stories.headline: World soccer's hottest men's teams right now: Can anyone stop Barcelona?
stories.summary: Is there any team hotter in world soccer right now than Barcelona? Bill Connelly crunches the numbers to tell us the most in-form European teams heading into the international break.
stories.body:
It's possible that no club in the world has had a better last three months or so than FC Barcelona. Hansi Flick's squad enjoyed a lovely 2025-26, winning LaLiga by eight points, scoring an all-time humiliation of Newcastle (by a 7-2 margin) in the second leg of the Champions League round of 16 and really only falling short of cup goals because of Atletico Madrid (who defeated them in both the Copa del Rey and Champions League).

Since that season ended, things have only improved. Eight Barcelona players were on Spain's World Cup winning squad -- six of them played in the final -- and when one left (Ferran Torres went to PSG), they added another (Rodri came over from Manchester City). They also added speedsters Anthony Gordon (a Flick player if ever one existed) and Karim Adeyemi.

Together, Barcelona have set the world alight to start 2026-27, outscoring their first seven opponents by a combined 33-7. Attackers Raphinha and Lamine Yamal have already combined for 19 goals and seven assists in all competitions; Gordon and Adeyemi have made immediate contributions, too, with three goals and six assists between them.

Barca haven't exactly faced a murderers' row to date -- the best opponent they've faced was world No. 69 Athletic Club, so says Opta's power ratings, and they're the only ones to hold Barca to fewer than four goals -- but their early form suggests they've either reestablished or topped their best run of form from last season. In fact, they enter the season's first international break as the hottest team in Europe.

- Marcotti: The staggering numbers behind Premier League's spending spree

- Hot Seat Index: Which coaches are at risk?

- Ogden: Soccer can learn from NFL when it comes to VAR

Every so often, I check in on teams' form over the last couple of months using what I call "adjusted goal differential" -- a mix of 30% goal differential and 70% xG differential in 11 vs. 11 situations. It isn't opponent-adjusted and therefore isn't intended to be predictive: it simply tells us who's in the hottest run of form. And based on league play, selected domestic cup play* and UEFA competitions, here are the 30 hottest teams from Europe's Big Five leagues since the start of the season.

(*Because there have still been quite a few matches between first-division and much lower-division clubs in the Coppa Italia and DFB Pokal, we'll only include the England's League Cup and the countries' various super cups ... for now. And we're awarding "points" for wins in different cups and competitions for illustrative effect.)

(Note: For each team's upcoming schedule, I've italicized the matches against other teams in this top 30 list)

1. Barcelona

The season thus far: 7 matches, 21 points (3.00 PPG), +3.06 adjusted goal differential (AGD) per game

The slate through October: at Sevilla (Sept. 19), Getafe (Oct. 10), at Galatasaray (Champions League, Oct. 13), at Real Betis (Oct. 18), at PSG* (Champions League, Oct. 20), Real Madrid (Oct. 25)

Sometimes the best moves are the ones fate saves you from making. With the departure of Robert Lewandowski, the club tried hard to add Atletico Madrid's Julián Álvarez over the summer for a ridiculous transfer fee, and there's no way he would have topped Raphinha's form. And while Alvarez's brightest moments could have won them some individual matches, going the route of increasing squad depth with players like Adeyemi and Gabriel Jesus (who has two goals and two chances created in just 37 minutes) might turn out to be more beneficial, too.

Everything's coming up Barca at the moment, and that might continue to be the case until late October. Then, we'll find out just how good they are when they battle both PSG and Real Madrid within six days of each other.

2. Bayern Munich

The season thus far: 5 matches, 13 points (2.60 PPG), +2.00 AGD

The slate through October: Union Berlin (Sept. 18), at Augsburg (Oct. 10), at Viking FK (Champions League, Oct. 13), RB Leipzig (Oct. 17), Arsenal (Champions League, Oct. 21), at Freiburg (Oct. 24), Magdeburg (DFB Pokal, Oct. 28), Borussia Dortmund (Oct. 31)

PSG might have been the only team capable of preventing Bayern from their first league, cup and Champions League treble in six years last season, but that gave Bayern something to remain hungry for in 2026-27. They've begun the season as dominant as ever, outscoring their first five opponents -- including Borussia Dortmund (in the Franz Beckenbauer Supercup), Bundesliga top-four contender VfB Stuttgart and giant killer Bodø/Glimt (in the Champions League) -- by a combined 14-3. They stumbled to a 0-0 draw at Schalke on September 5, but that was an xG special: They attempted 15 shots worth 1.9 xG, but somehow none went in the net.

Harry Kane has encountered the slightest of finishing funks: He has scored two goals from shots worth 2.22 xG after going for 61 goals from 44.3 xG last year. But Michael Olise is as ruthless as ever, new addition Ismael Saibari has two assists from five chances created in just 185 minutes, and Lennart Karl has added a goal and an assist in 138 minutes.

Saibari, Karl and an improving Jamal Musiala should give Bayern even better attacking depth than they had last season, which could help to assure that Kane, Olise and Luis Díaz are in the form they need to be in when the Champions League knockouts roll around.

3. Real Madrid

The season thus far: 7 matches, 18 points (2.57 PPG), +1.91 adj. GD

The slate through October: at Atletico Madrid (Sept. 20), Villarreal (Oct. 10), at Roma (Champions League, Oct. 14), Sevilla (Oct. 18), RB Leipzig (Champions League, Oct. 21), at Barcelona (Oct. 25)

This has quickly shaped up to be one of those seasons in which only Barca and Real Madrid have much to offer in Spain. Real Betis were the only other team to win their first Champions League match of the season -- Atletico Madrid and Villarreal both faded against Liverpool and Borussia Dortmund, respectively -- and Betis incredibly have the third-best points-per-game average despite just a plus-1 goal differential. The league's two dominant forces have combined to drop two points in 12 matches.

From an entertainment standpoint, it's always more fun when someone else is along for the ride, even if it's just Atletico Madrid (who have already dropped five points in league play). Then again, maybe Jose Mourinho's return to Real Madrid has already maxed out the drama quota.

Mourinho has been mostly quiet thus far, but while Real Madrid have battled through some wobbly road performances, their home form has been indomitable. They've won four matches in the Bernebeu by a combined 14-3, and while sideline drama is eventually inevitable with Mourinho, he thus far has his team running and defending in a way Xabi Alonso certainly couldn't figure out last year. And his occasionally transition-heavy style was always going to fit well with Kylian Mbappé, who has eight goals and two assists from 12 chances created in seven matches.

4. Roma

The season thus far: 5 matches, 13 points (2.60 PPG), +1.69 adj. GD

The slate through October: Inter Milan (Sept. 19), at Como (Oct. 11), Real Madrid (Champions League, Oct. 14), Genoa (Oct. 17), Slovan Bratislava (Champions League, Oct. 20), at Napoli (Oct. 24), Cagliari (Oct. 27), at Udinese (Oct. 31)

Manager Gian Piero Gasperini deploys one of the most exciting and aesthetically pleasing styles in the sport, and his second Roma team has been nearly perfect thus far. They've beaten four Serie A opponents by a combined 12-1, and their only hiccup was a 1-1 draw at Fenerbahce in their Champions League opener. Donyell Malen has been engaged and prolific (six goals and an assist in five matches), and Paulo Dybala has been at his creative best (four goals from 18 chances created).

We'll see if they have the depth to maintain this level through their first Champions League campaign since 2018-19, but they've been the best team in Italy out of the gate.

5. Bayer Leverkusen

The season thus far: 4 matches, 7 points (1.75 PPG), +1.40 adj. GD

The slate through October: RB Leipzig (Sept. 20), at Mainz 05 (Oct. 10), at Lech Poznan (Europa League, Oct. 15), Freiburg (Oct. 17), at OFI Creta (Europa League, Oct. 22), at Hoffenheim (Oct. 24), Nürnberg (DFB Pokal, Oct. 28), VfB Stuttgart (Oct. 31)

Here's the first surprise. Leverkusen have won only once in three Bundesliga matches, suffering a 3-2 loss to newcomers Elversberg and settling for a 2-2 draw with Augsburg last weekend. But their underlying xG numbers say these were pretty unfortunate results. Elversberg and Augsburg scored their five goals from shots worth just 2.4 xG, and combined with a 4-0 trouncing of Union Berlin, Leverkusen have created far more quality chances than their opponents thus far. Over the course of the season, their point total will probably reflect that.

New left back Miguel Gutierrez is forming a nice creative partnership with 20-year-old Ibrahim Maza -- including a DFB Pokal win, the two have combined for a goal and four assists from 21 chances created thus far -- and new manager Carles Martinez is coaxing solid production from other youngsters like Christian Kofane (20) and Afonso Moreira (21).

6. Arsenal

The season thus far: 7 matches, 21 points (3.00 PPG), +1.36 adj. GD

The slate through October: at Brighton (Sept. 19), Leeds United (Oct. 10), Lille (Champions League, Oct. 13), at Nottingham Forest (Oct. 18), at Bayern Munich (Champions League, Oct. 21), Everton (Oct. 24)

Safe to say, if we adjusted these stats for opponent strength, Arsenal would shoot to No. 1. They've already played (and beaten) Manchester City in the Community Shield and Chelsea in the Premier League, and their next competitive loss will be their first since the Champions League final against PSG. (And technically, that was a draw until the shootout.) They were the best team in the world's best league last season, and they've only gotten better and deeper with the additions of veterans Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa and thrilling winger Christos Tzolis, who's already created four assists from 13 chances created in 420 minutes.

As with Barcelona, they might have been saved from themselves in failing to land Real Madrid's Vinícius Júnior, who obviously would have raised their ceiling, but might have altered their defensive structure at the same time. Regardless, it's impossible to bet against them in any given match right now, just as it was for almost all of last season.

7. Inter Milan

The season thus far: 5 matches, 12 points (2.40 PPG), +1.12 adj. GD

The slate through October: at Roma (Sept. 19), Parma (Oct. 10), Club Brugge (Champions League, Oct. 13), at Bologna (Oct. 17), Shakhtar Donetsk (Champions League, Oct. 21), Fiorentina (Oct. 25), at Venezia (Oct. 28), at AC Milan (Oct. 31)

Among the Champions League teams on this list, maybe no one has a more manageable October than Inter -- they face an enormous trip to Rome this weekend, but should rack up points after the international break. Inter couldn't quite come back against Real Madrid in the Champions League, but this attack is working exactly as it should, with attackers Lautaro Martínez, Marcus Thuram and Francesco Esposito combining for 49 shots worth 7.9 xG (though they've only managed six goals) and midfielders Andy Diouf, Federico Dimarco and Nicolò Barella combining for five assists from 41 chances created.

When their finishing improves, Inter might become unstoppable in Italy.

8. Paris FC

The season thus far: 4 matches, 8 points (2.00 PPG), +1.12 adj. GD

The slate through October: Strasbourg (Sept. 19), at Lorient (Oct. 10), Rennes (Oct. 18), at Lens (Oct. 24)

What a start the other Paris club has enjoyed. They're unbeaten through four Ligue 1 matches and were unfortunate to draw with Troyes in the opener (xG: Paris 1.8, Troyes 0.4). They pummeled Nice and won at Marseille for the first time ever. New addition Lassine Sinayoko has been a game-changer in attack, and Paris are both third in Ligue 1 in xG per shot and first in xG allowed. Creating all the good shots will win you lots of matches.

9. Brentford

The season thus far: 6 matches, 12 points (2.00 PPG), +1.05 adj. GD

The slate through October: Chelsea (Sept. 18), at Aston Villa (Oct. 10), Liverpool (Oct. 17), at Hull City (Oct. 25), Nottingham Forest (Oct. 31)

Granted, they've been settling for too many draws of late to fulfill my "Brentford to the Champions League" bold prediction, but Brentford have yet to lose in any competition this season, but new defensive midfielder Mamadou Sangare has been a game-changer, and as soon as Igor Thiago remembers how to finish -- he has one goal from shots worth 3.7 xG -- the draws could turn back into wins.

10. SC Freiburg

The season thus far: 5 matches, 15 points (3.00 PPG), +1.05 adj. GD

The slate through October: at Eintracht Frankfurt (Sept. 19), Schalke 04 (Oct. 10), FK Jablonec (Conference League, Oct. 15), at Bayer Leverkusen (Oct. 17), at Monaco (Oct. 22), Bayern Munich (Oct. 24), Wolfsburg (DFB Pokal, Oct. 28), at Augsburg (Oct. 31)

Freiburg are basically Germany's Bournemouth or Brighton -- they lose young stars and keep getting better.

Including Conference League qualification and the DFB Pokal, they've begun this season a perfect 6-for-6 in the wins department despite losing up-and-comer Johan Manzambi to Aston Villa, and the new attacking partnership of Igor Matanovic (23), Derry Scherhant (23) and Yuito Suzuki (24) has combined for 10 goals and seven assists from 30 chances created. Noah Atubolu, the best young keeper in Germany, left for Eintracht Frankfurt, but Mio Backhaus (22) has allowed just four goals in seven matches and has kept two straight clean sheets.

11. Mainz

The season thus far: 3 matches, 4 points (1.33 PPG), +1.04 adj. GD

The slate through October: at Borussia Mönchengladbach (Sept. 19), Bayer Leverkusen (Oct. 10), at Schalke 04 (Oct. 17), Werder Bremen (Oct. 24), at Bochum (DFB Pokal, Oct. 27), at Elversberg (Oct. 31)

When Urs Fischer arrived at Mainz last December, they were in last place in the Bundesliga. They've been in top-half-of-the-table form since. They've been unlucky to start 2026-27, suffering both a draw (to Paderborn) and loss (to Eintracht Frankfurt) despite generating a positive xG differential in every game, but veterans Phillip Tietz (seven goals in all competitions) and Nadiem Amiri (two goals and two assists from 20 chances created) have been excellent, and you know Fischer, who brought Union Berlin to the Champions League, will always have a team that runs and defends hard.

12. Paris Saint-Germain

The season thus far: 6 matches, 8 points (1.33 PPG), +1.00 adj. GD

The slate through October: at Marseille (Sept. 20), Le Mans (Oct. 10), at Manchester City (Champions League, Oct. 14), at Strasbourg (Oct. 17), Barcelona (Champions League, Oct. 20), Lyon (Oct. 25)

Finally we get to PSG, the second French team -- nay, the second Parisien team -- on the list. We saw PSG sleepwalk through the fall months and then casually ignite to win another Champions League (and Ligue 1) title, and they're obviously capable of doing so again. But they were even sleepier to start this season, losing to Lens in the Trophée des Champions and then taking just two points from their first three Ligue 1 matches.

Granted, they had at least a slightly positive xG differential in every match, and they stomped Slovan Bratislava to start Champions League play. Luis Enrique has already started 19 different players. It's hard to actually pretend to worry about them eventually reaching championship form again, but they've given themselves some work to do -- domestically, at least.

13. Como

The season thus far: 5 matches, 13 points (2.60 PPG), +0.97 adj. GD

The slate through October: at Frosinone (Sept. 20), Roma (Oct. 11), at Feyenoord (Champions League, Oct. 14), at Fiorentina (Oct. 18), Manchester United (Champions League, Oct. 21), Sassuolo (Oct. 24), at Torino (Oct. 27)

Como may have provided the most delightful moment of Champions League Matchday 1, manhandling RB Leipzig 4-1 for their first ever win in the competition. They're also unbeaten in Serie A, getting creative contributions from pretty much the entire (young) lineup. Looking at expected goals and assists (xG+xA), nine different players are between 0.9 and 2.4 right now, and eight of them are aged 25 or younger.

There's no other way to say it: You really need to be watching Cesc Fabregas' squad.

14. Juventus

The season thus far: 4 matches, 7 points (1.75 PPG), +0.97 adj. GD

The slate through October: NEC Nijmegen (Europa League, Sept. 17), Atalanta (Sept. 20), at Cagliari (Oct. 11), at Celta de Vigo (Europa League, Oct. 15), Lazio (Oct. 18), Rennes (Europa League, Oct. 22), at Lecce (Oct. 25), at Genoa (Oct. 28)

Luciano Spalletti is working about eight newcomers into his rotation and has only Europa League play to worry about as he attempts to build Juve back into a Champions League-caliber squad. The results have been scattershot -- they drew with AC Milan and lost a wild one at Sassuolo last week -- but they've generated a positive xG differential in every match, and they're both pressing and tilting the pitch well.

Shot quality is a problem -- they're 17th in Serie A in xG per shot -- but trends are somewhere between fine and good.

15. Everton

The season thus far: 6 matches, 12 points (2.00 PPG), +0.91 adj. GD

The slate through October: Ipswich Town (Sept. 19), at Hull City (Oct. 11), Chelsea (Oct. 17), at Arsenal (Oct. 24)

Like Brentford, Everton are settling for too many draws -- three straight at the moment -- and including League Cup stats means including two wins (by a combined 5-0) over second-division teams, which got them on this list. So their spot is a bit inflated here, but they're playing at a solid mid-table level in the Premier League, and they're counterattacking with abandon.

In other words: they're a David Moyes team.

16. Brighton & Hove Albion

The season thus far: 7 matches, 14 points (2.00 PPG), +0.90 AGD

The slate through October: Arsenal (Sept. 19), at Sunderland (Oct. 10), FK Kauno Zalgiris (Conference League, Oct. 15), Crystal Palace (Oct. 18), at FK Jablonec (Conference League, Oct. 22), at Liverpool (Oct. 25), at Manchester City (Oct. 31)

It's at least a slight concern that Brighton have taken only one point against the two best teams they've faced in league play -- Chelsea (lost 4-3) and Leeds (drew 1-1), both of whom won the xG battle -- but they overcame a 2-0 deficit to win a wild League Cup match at Man United on Wednesday, and you can rack up a nice point total by beating the teams you're supposed to beat. Including Conference League qualification, Brighton have beaten four other opponents by a combined 13-0. Veteran Pascal Gross is playing as well as ever, 19-year-old defender Luka Vuskovic has been an immediate hit, and another teenager, 2025 addition Charalampos Kostoulas, is starting to contribute too.

17. Brest

The season thus far: 4 matches, 5 points (1.25 PPG), +0.83 adj. GD)

The slate through October: at AJ Auxerre (Sept. 20), Angers (Oct. 10), at Lille (Oct. 17), Nice (Oct. 23)

Almost no one in Europe has gotten xG'd harder than Brest, who have created most of the good chances in their matches (xG: Brest 9.5, opponents 4.8) but haven't turned that into many points (actual goals: 6-6). They were solid in last week's 1-0 loss to PSG, as soon as anyone besides 23-year-old star Kamory Doumbia begins to actually shoot accurately, this team could fulfill its top-four potential.

18. Manchester United

The season thus far: 6 matches, 7 points (1.17 PPG), +0.78 adj. GD

The slate through October: at Fulham (Sept. 20), Tottenham Hotspur (Oct. 10), at Atletico Madrid (Champions League, Oct. 13), at Leeds United (Oct. 18), at Como (Champions League, Oct. 21), Bournemouth (Oct. 25), at Chelsea (Oct. 31)

Like Bayer Leverkusen, United's underlying numbers are a little better than their raw results to date, thanks primarily to dominant performances against Ipswich and Sabah. They've lost to Hull and Manchester City (technically, in the latter case) and were inferior in a 2-2 draw with Everton.

Bryan Mbeumo, Matheus Cunha and Marcus Rashford have all struggled in the finishing department -- they've combined for three goals from shots worth 5.2 xG (ironic, considering United acquired Mbeumo and Cunha when they were at their highest value following overachievement in the finishing department) -- but when that form rebounds, and when Michael Carrick is able to work newcomer Carlos Baleba into the rotation, United's results should pick up quickly.

19. RB Leipzig

The season thus far: 4 matches, 6 points (1.50 PPG), +0.77 adj. GD

The slate through October: at Bayer Leverkusen (Sept. 20), Eintracht Frankfurt (Oct. 10), PSV Eindhoven (Champions League, Oct. 13), at Bayern Munich (Oct. 17), at Real Madrid (Champions League, Oct. 21), Elversberg (Oct. 21), at RW Essen (DFB Pokal, Oct. 27), at Schalke (Oct. 31)

Either it all works or it all doesn't for RB Leipzig, who have played two brilliant Bundesliga matches (they beat Borussia Mönchengladbach and Hamburg by a combined 8-0) and pummeled lower-level Eintracht Trier 6-0 in the DFB Pokal but also lost 3-1 to Werder Bremen and got thumped by Como in the Champions League. They are playing like the high-octane set of youngsters that they are. But even with inconsistency, the foursome of Antonio Nusa (21), Ezechiel Banzuzi (21), Brajan Gruda (22) and Tidiam Gomis (20) has already given them a combined six goals and seven assists from 27 chances created.

We'll see if they're up for a pretty ridiculous run of October matches.

20. Manchester City

The season thus far: 6 matches, 15 points (2.50 PPG), +0.77 adj. GD

The slate through October: Norwich City (League Cup, Sept. 17), Sunderland (Sept. 20), at Liverpool (Oct. 11), PSG (Champions League, Oct. 14), Ipswich Town (Oct. 17), AEK Athens (Champions League, Oct. 20), at Aston Villa (Oct. 24), Brighton (Oct. 31)

Finally we get to Manchester City, whose average here was hit pretty hard by a dreadful Community Shield performance against Arsenal. That 3-0 loss, followed by a poor start against Bournemouth, dragged them down, but they've been excellent ever since, coming back to beat Bournemouth late and winning all four matches since.

Erling Haaland has the customary six goals in six matches, Rayan Cherki and Antoine Semenyo have four assists from 23 chances created, and newcomers Elliot Anderson and Iliman Ndiaye have provided exactly what they've been asked for so far -- linebreaking passes from the former, duels and ball recoveries from the latter.

stories.headline: Enforcer Ryan Reaves retires; just 3 visor-less NHL players left
stories.summary: Ryan Reaves said Wednesday he is retiring from hockey at age 39 after playing more than a decade and a half in the NHL.
stories.body:
Enforcer Ryan Reaves said Wednesday he is retiring from hockey at age 39 after playing more than a decade and a half in the NHL, leaving just three players left who do not wear a visor.

Reaves skated in 1,075 games from his debut in 2010 through last season and racked up 1,253 penalty minutes, playing for St. Louis, Pittsburgh, Vegas, the New York Rangers, Minnesota and Toronto. His 3,225 hits rank seventh on the all-time list.

The tough-guy forward announced he was calling it a career in an Instagram post.

"Unfortunately, Father Time remains undefeated," Reaves wrote. "Every hit, every fight -- it's taken its final toll on me. I love this sport more than almost anything in this world. It has taken me to places I never thought I'd go and has introduced me to people I'll cherish for the rest of my life. The fans, the haters, the ups, the downs. I wouldn't trade it for anything.

"I never thought this day would come. I thought I was invincible. I thought I could play forever, but like all good things, it must come to an end."

Reaves, an imposing figure at 6-foot-2 and 225 pounds, fittingly ended the post with: "You can rest easy knowing the corners are a little safer today. Mic drop, gloves drop. Reavo out."

A Winnipeg, Manitoba, native, Reaves was a fifth-round pick of the Blues in 2005. He grinded through several years in the minors, earning a call-up for his toughness and eventually leadership that helped him stick at the highest level of the sport.

Nashville's Ryan O'Reilly, Dallas' Jamie Benn and Minnesota's Zach Bogosian are the final remaining no-visor players. The NHL and NHL Players' Association agreed in 2013 to mandate visors for newcomers, grandfathering them like helmets were decades earlier.

stories.headline: WNBA playoff picture 2026: What's on the line in final week?
stories.summary: The WNBA playoff teams are set, but all eight seeds are up for grabs before the regular season ends Sept. 24.
stories.body:
Celebrations for the medalists at the FIBA Women's World Cup -- the United States, France and Spain -- are done. It's time for WNBA players to get back to work.

The league restarts its 30th season Thursday and finishes the regular-season schedule on Sept. 24. All 15 teams have four games left. The eight playoff teams are already set, but the seeding order remains undecided. The WNBA playoffs open Sept. 27.

The place to be is in the top-four seeds. That provides a home-court edge, hosting the first and potential third games in the best-of-three first round. The semifinals are best-of-five affairs, and the WNBA Finals are best-of-seven.

The league-leading Minnesota Lynx are in the strongest position, guaranteed either the No. 1 or No. 2 seed. The Golden State Valkyries are the only team that can catch the Lynx for No. 1. If they don't, the Valkyries are the favorites for No. 2.

Three other teams still have a chance at the No. 2 seed, although they are longshots according to ESPN Analytics: the defending champion Las Vegas Aces, the Atlanta Dream and the Indiana Fever.

The other playoff teams -- the New York Liberty, the Washington Mystics and the Dallas Wings -- remain in the running for the top four, but the odds are stacked against them.

There is still a lot on the line as some teams battle for playoff position while others try to finish their seasons on a high note. Here's how the playoff picture looks as the season resumes.

Top candidates for Nos. 1 and 2 seeds

Minnesota Lynx (31-9)

Highest potential seed: 1

Lowest potential seed: 2

Remaining games: vs. NY (Sept. 18), @ CON (Sept. 20), @ IND (Sept. 22), vs. IND (Sept. 24)

Outlook: The Lynx lost their last two games before the FIBA World Cup break -- to Golden State and at Atlanta -- but won 16 of 17 before that. Minnesota has a two-game lead in first place over Golden State. The Lynx have the tiebreaker against the Valkyries, having won the season series 3-1, so Golden State must finish ahead of Minnesota in the standings to claim the top seed.

The Lynx are in the driver's seat: If they win at least two of their last four games, they will be the No. 1 seed for the second season in a row, regardless of how Golden State finishes. And the worst the Lynx can do is the No. 2 seed. That's because even if the Lynx lose their last four games, they also have the tiebreaker against Las Vegas, the only other team besides Golden State that could match Minnesota's record.

As for the opponents Minnesota has left, the Lynx split their two games against New York and Connecticut and won their only matchup with Indiana. So while the odds favor the Lynx, they still must take care of business. Rookie of the Year shoo-in Olivia Miles got some needed rest during the FIBA World Cup break, and Napheesa Collier rejoins the Lynx with a gold medal.

Golden State Valkyries (29-11)

Highest potential seed: 1

Lowest potential seed: 5

Remaining games: vs. POR (Sept. 18), vs. SEA (Sept. 19), @ POR (Sept. 22), @ LA (Sept. 24)

Outlook: The Valkyries are in just their second season of existence and have made the playoffs both years. Last season, they were the No. 8 seed. Now they are still in play for No. 1, and if they fall short of that the odds are in their favor for No. 2.

The Valkyries must pass the Lynx in the standings for the top seed since the Lynx have the season series tiebreaker. Thus, even if Golden State wins out, the Valkyries still need the Lynx to lose three of their last four. However, with two victories, Golden State can do no worse than the No. 2 seed.

The Valkyries' remaining games are against teams that are not in the playoffs. However, Golden State will be on the road for the last two. The finale is at Los Angeles and will be Sparks star Nneka Ogwumike's final game before she retires from the WNBA, so the Valkyries must overcome that emotion.

Top candidate for No. 3 seed

Las Vegas Aces (27-13)

Highest potential seed: 2

Lowest potential seed: 8

Remaining games: @ SEA (Sept. 17), vs. SEA (Sept. 20), vs. LA (Sept. 22), @ PHO (Sept. 24)

Outlook: The defending champion Aces still have a slim chance -- 4%, according to ESPN Analytics -- at grabbing the No. 2 seed. The No. 3 seed is more likely. While they could still drop as low as No. 8, there is a 96.4% chance they will be in the top four. Four-time MVP A'ja Wilson, dealing with back issues, didn't go to the World Cup and had time to recuperate. Aces guards Jackie Young and Chelsea Gray both won gold.

Las Vegas' remaining games are against teams that are not in the playoffs. Two are vs. Seattle, which lost forward Ezi Magbegor (Australia) to a knee injury suffered during the World Cup.

Top candidates for No. 4 seed

Atlanta Dream (26-14)

Highest potential seed: 2

Lowest potential seed: 8

Remaining games: vs. CON (Sept. 17), vs. CHI (Sept. 19), @ NY (Sept. 21), @ NY (Sept. 23)

Outlook: According to ESPN Analytics, the Dream and Fever have about a 1% chance of getting the No. 2 seed; that would take a collapse from Golden State. It's more likely that they will be battling for No. 4. The Dream (49.7%) have slightly better odds than Indiana (44.7%) of getting into the top four. Both teams have the same record, and they tied 2-2 in their regular-season series. The difference could be that Atlanta has a little easier schedule the rest of the way. The Fever beat the Dream 2-1 in the first round of the playoffs last season. The Dream's Rhyne Howard and Angel Reese came home from the World Cup with gold medals.

Indiana Fever (26-14)

Highest potential seed: 2

Lowest potential seed: 8

Remaining games: @ TOR (Sept. 18), vs. WAS (Sept. 20), vs. MIN (Sept. 22), @ MIN (Sept. 24)

Outlook: The Fever were the No. 6 seed during the past two years and didn't make the playoffs in the seven seasons before that. This year, according to ESPN Analytics, Atlanta has a 5% better chance than Indiana to get one of the top four seeds, so this could be a battle to the wire. Indiana won seven of its past nine contests before the FIBA World Cup break, and Aliyah Boston and Caitlin Clark won gold with Team USA. Now, they hope to bring back that energy. Three of Indiana's remaining games are against playoff teams, including two against league-leading Minnesota.

Longest shots to be in top-four seeds

New York Liberty (24-16)

Highest potential seed: 3

Lowest potential seed: 8

Remaining games: @ MIN (Sept. 18), @ TOR (Sept. 20), vs. ATL (Sept. 21), vs. ATL (Sept. 23)

Outlook: New York has been one of the most challenging teams to predict this season, going 4-3 in its past seven games before the World Cup break. But three Liberty players -- Team USA's Breanna Stewart and France's Pauline Astier and Marine Johannes -- played in the World Cup gold medal game and should bring back some positive momentum to the Liberty. According to ESPN Analytics, the Liberty have just a 5.1% chance of getting into the top-four seeds. Three of New York's remaining opponents are playoff teams, with a lot on the line for the Liberty and Atlanta in their last two regular-season games, both in Brooklyn.

Washington Mystics (24-16)

Highest potential seed: 3

Lowest potential seed: 8

Remaining games: @ CHI (Sept. 17), @ IND (Sept. 20), vs. CON (Sept. 22), vs. CHI (Sept. 24)

Outlook: This season is a big success for the young Mystics regardless of their playoff seed. Few expected them to make the 2026 postseason. Sonia Citron and Kiki Iriafen, in their second WNBA season, were part of the U.S. World Cup team.

ESPN Analytics gives Washington a 2.8% chance to be in the top-four seeds. But the Mystics own the tiebreaker against Dallas, which could help them stay out of the No. 8 spot. Just one of their remaining games is against a playoff team (Indiana). Washington still has two games against Chicago; the Mystics beat the Sky in their earlier matchup this season in June.

Dallas Wings (24-16)

Highest potential seed: 3

Lowest potential seed: 8

Remaining games: vs. LA (Sept. 17), vs. PHO (Sept. 19), @ PHO (Sept. 21), @ SEA (Sept. 23)

Outlook: Like the Mystics, the Wings are back in the postseason after missing the playoffs the past two years. No. 1 draft pick Azzi Fudd is out the rest of the season due to a knee injury. But 2025 top pick and Rookie of the Year Paige Bueckers leads the Wings in scoring and assists. She is coming off a gold medal with the U.S. World Cup team. Dallas has the tiebreaker against New York, but Washington has it against Dallas. And while the Wings' remaining games are all against teams out of the playoffs, finishing on the road at Phoenix and Seattle still could be a challenge.

stories.headline: NBA offseason recap, early 2026-27 season previews by team
stories.summary: We're looking back at the offseason and taking an early look at the regular season by rolling out one team profile each weekday through Sept. 18.
stories.body:
After an eventful July full of big trades, intriguing signings and the game's biggest star shocking everyone by heading East, the NBA offseason is nearly complete. And with the regular-season schedule now out, it's time to start thinking about the 2026-27 season.

ESPN's staff of experts is looking back at the offseason and taking an early look at the season for all 30 teams, with 30 pieces -- one for every team -- rolling out each weekday through Sept. 18. We're answering the biggest looming questions, evaluating X factors and much more for every team.

Check out the rollout schedule below, with stories added daily:

Quick links:

Free agency buzz | FA grades | Trade grades

Transactions | Schedule | More NBA coverage

Atlantic Division

Philadelphia 76ers: Sept. 14
Key additions: F LeBron James, G Jaylen Brown, G Anfernee Simons, F Dean Wade, G Labaron Philon Jr., G Kentavious Caldwell-Pope

Key subtractions: F Paul George, C Andre Drummond, G Quentin Grimes, G Kelly Oubre Jr.

No team changed its fortunes from April to July as drastically as the 76ers. Taking advantage of Boston's desire to get out of the Jaylen Brown business enabled it to accomplish so much: getting a motivated All-Star feeling the sting of rejection following a career year, dumping George's contract and putting themselves in position to be attractive to an all-time great in James, who was looking for a new challenge. They also lessened their dependency on Joel Embiid's bothersome health as he will turn 33 during the season.

They filled in the blanks by adding Caldwell-Pope and Wade as plug-and-play wings, changing the complexion of their franchise in several swoops. If nothing else, they won the offseason. -- Vincent Goodwill

Read the full 76ers offseason recap/season preview

Boston Celtics: Sept. 15
Key additions: Paul George, Mitchell Robinson, Mike Conley

Key subtractions: Jaylen Brown, Nikola Vucevic

Key retentions: Neemias Queta, Jordan Walsh, Ron Harper Jr.

Boston responded to its first early playoff exit since 2021 by boldly trading Brown to the 76ers, ending his fruitful partnership with Jayson Tatum. The move should improve the Celtics' long-term flexibility to build around Tatum, but next year's iteration will require the aging George to discover the fountain of youth. The 36-year-old forward has played in 60 games just once in the past seven seasons.

Even so, this shouldn't be viewed as a gap year. The Celtics return a cohesive nucleus, and they added Robinson's defense and rebounding to shore up a frontcourt rotation that was overwhelmed in the postseason.

If Tatum returns to superstar form in his first fully healthy season since a May 2025 Achilles injury, the Celtics will have a chance to win at least 50 games for the sixth straight year. Securing Banner 19, however, will likely require finding a superstar replacement for Brown sometime down the road. -- Ben Golliver

Read the full Celtics offseason recap/season preview

Brooklyn Nets: Sept. 16
Key additions: F Julius Randle, G Mikel Brown Jr., G Keon Ellis

Key subtractions: C Nic Claxton

Key retentions: C Day'Ron Sharpe, F Josh Minott

Once commissioner Adam Silver responded to last season's shameless tankathon by nearly a third of the league's teams by implementing a draft lottery reform, the Nets could no longer slow-play their rebuild by hoping for ping-pong luck. Getting Randle back to New York, but this time across town from his former team, and one he watched win an NBA championship without him, was a big move for the Nets. Plus, drafting a promising point guard, Brown at No. 6, in this year's draft adds to a glut of guards on the roster, but the Nets were in serious need of a talent upgrade across the board. Even with the addition of Randle, who's due to make $33.3 million this season, the Nets are still well below the salary cap, meaning they can take in plenty of money in deals should the opportunity present itself. -- Vincent Goodwill

Read the full Nets offseason recap/season preview

Toronto Raptors: Sept. 17
Key additions: Kawhi Leonard, Kyle Anderson, Andre Jackson Jr.

Key subtractions: Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, Sandro Mamukelashvili

Key retentions: Jamal Shead

After waiting months to finalize their acquisition of Leonard from the Clippers due to the NBA's investigation into salary cap circumvention, the Raptors can finally look ahead to what could be their most promising season in years.

Leonard, who led Toronto to the 2019 championship, plugs in as a major positional upgrade over Ingram. The rest of the Raptors' starting lineup remains intact, and forward Collin Murray-Boyles should only improve after a standout rookie campaign.

While losing Mamukelashvili in free agency took a bite out of their bench unit, Toronto has crafted a high-energy and versatile supporting cast for Leonard and two-time All-Star Scottie Barnes.

The plucky Raptors, who won 46 games last season, have a real shot to win their first playoff series since 2020. -- Ben Golliver

Read the full Raptors offseason recap/season preview

New York Knicks: Sept. 18

h2>Central Division

Milwaukee Bucks: Sept. 7
Key additions: Tyler Herro, Kel'el Ware, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kasparas Jakucionis, Caris LeVert

Key retentions: Gary Trent Jr.

Key subtractions: Giannis Antetokounmpo, Bobby Portis

After 13 seasons, the Giannis era ended in Milwaukee with a mega trade to the Heat -- and the 2026-27 season will mark a major shift for the rebuilding franchise.

The Bucks hired coach Taylor Jenkins to establish a culture. They added four new players from Miami, including former All-Star and Wisconsin native Tyler Herro, and selected Brayden Burries with the No. 10 pick in June.

The Bucks will enter the season with an ill-fitting mix of players and low expectations, but they have the luxury to see what sticks long term. -- Jamal Collier

Read the full Bucks offseason recap/season preview

Chicago Bulls: Sept. 8
Key additions: F Caleb Wilson, G Dailyn Swain, C Nic Claxton, G Norman Powell, Tiago Splitter

Key subtractions: None

Key retentions: F Zach Collins

For years, Chicago has been seen as one of the sleeping giants of the NBA, a once-proud franchise reduced to meandering in the play-in tournament and in the middle of the lottery in recent seasons. But the Bulls got a much-needed makeover this summer and enter the 2026-27 season with a clearer direction than they've had in years.

The changes have been full-scale: Bryson Graham was hired as the team's new head of basketball operations, Tiago Splitter will patrol the sidelines as head coach, No. 4 pick Caleb Wilson is the new face of the franchise, and he'll be surrounded by some veterans like Nic Claxton and Norman Powell to help ease his transition. -- Jamal Collier

Read the full Bulls offseason recap/season preview

Cleveland Cavaliers: Sept. 9
Key additions: Peyton Watson, Mario Hezonja

Key subtractions: Dean Wade, Dennis Schroder, Max Strus, Larry Nance Jr., Caris Levert, Keon Ellis

Key retentions: Donovan Mitchell, James Harden

The Cavs' failed pursuit of LeBron James this summer turned into a pivot for a younger, athletic wing, prying Watson from the Nuggets after a career-year.

Watson averaged career highs in points, rebounds, assists and steals while shooting 41% from 3 last year, and he has in recent years been one of the strongest wing defenders in the league. That makes him a strong complement next to James Harden and Donovan Mitchell, as the Cavs hope he can provide a substantial answer to the elusive fifth starter role next to their core four. -- Jamal Collier

Read the full Cavaliers offseason recap/season preview

Detroit Pistons: Sept. 10
Key additions: John Collins, Isaiah Joe, Taurean Prince, Gary Harris

Key subtractions: Tobias Harris, Isaiah Stewart

Key retentions: None

The Pistons' offseason is still in limbo as negotiations with restricted free agent Jalen Duren have stalled.

Detroit believes it sent Duren a fair offer considering the totality of his 2025-26 season -- including his underwhelming playoff showing -- while Duren feels like he's checked off all the boxes to get more.

Losing Harris and Stewart will be a big test to their culture -- or a signal they have to win a different way than in the last two seasons.

They added shooting on the margins with Joe, Prince and Harris. And assuming Duren's deal gets done before camp, Ausar Thompson's contract is next on the docket. -- Vincent Goodwill

Read the full Pistons offseason recap/season preview

Indiana Pacers: Sept. 11
Key additions: Kelly Oubre Jr., Larry Nance Jr.

Key retentions: None

Key subtractions: C Micah Potter

The Pacers didn't make any major offseason changes, but they will have two major additions to the roster they were missing last year: starting center Ivica Zubac, who was acquired at the trade deadline from the Clippers, and star guard Tyrese Haliburton, returning from injury for the first time since the 2025 NBA Finals.

Haliburton's presence lifted the Pacers into an Eastern Conference contender in 2024 and '25, and 16 months after a torn Achilles, they'll be counting on him to do the same in 2027. And Zubac will provide a different kind of center than Myles Turner provided the last time Haliburton was on the court. -- Jamal Collier

Read the full offseason recap/season preview

Southeast Division

Miami Heat: Aug. 31
Key additions: Giannis Antetokounmpo, Klay Thompson, Bobby Portis, Tim Hardaway Jr., Nick Richards

Key retentions: Andrew Wiggins, Simone Fontecchio

Key subtractions: Tyler Herro, Norman Powell, Kel'el Ware, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kasparas Jakucionis

Heat president Pat Riley landed the superstar he'd been searching for since LeBron James left Miami in 2016. Antetokounmpo is in the fold, and Miami is ready to contend for another title with the two-time MVP. Antetokounmpo is just as motivated to win his second title and remind everyone that he can be the best player in the league.

In the trade, the Heat gave up key players such as Herro, Ware and Jaquez and did not bring back Powell in free agency. They landed Thompson to a two-year, $13 million deal after the four-time champion sharpshooter worked out a buyout with the Dallas Mavericks. Miami also added Portis and Hardaway, but the team is still looking to bolster the roster around Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo. -- Ohm Youngmisuk

Read the full Heat offseason recap/season preview

Washington Wizards: Sept. 1
Key additions: AJ Dybantsa, Khris Middleton, Deandre Ayton, Tre Mann

Key subtractions: Cam Whitmore, D'Angelo Russell, Jaden Hardy

Key retentions: Trae Young

The Wizards got their jump on this pivotal offseason by acquiring Trae Young and Anthony Davis last season in trades.

Those were their two big moves and then came the big prize for losing 65 games last season - winning the lottery and drafting AJ Dybantsa with the first overall pick.

Ready to start winning games this season after losing 60 or more games in each of the past three years, Washington gave Young a four-year, $212 million contract. The Wizards added veterans like Khris Middleton and Deandre Ayton to bolster the depth behind their young core featuring the likes of Dybantsa, Alex Sarr, Kyshawn George, Tre Johnson and Will Riley. -- Ohm Youngmisuk

Read the full Wizards offseason recap/season preview

Charlotte Hornets: Sept. 2
Key additions: F Naz Reid, G Grayson Allen, G Dennis Schroder, F Royce O'Neale, F Dorian Finney-Smith

Key retentions: G Coby White

Key subtractions: G LaMelo Ball, F Miles Bridges, G Josh Green, G Tre Mann

After enjoying their best season in a decade, the Hornets sharply changed course with the surprising decision to trade Ball, their franchise guard, to the Timberwolves.

Given that Ball was a borderline All-Star on a max contract, Charlotte opted for a "Moneyball" approach in hopes of avoiding the perpetual mediocrity that tripped up Trae Young's Atlanta Hawks in the recent past.

With Ball and starting forward Miles Bridges moved in separate deals aimed at collecting future draft assets and improving its cap flexibility, Charlotte is now the only team that doesn't have a single player on the books for at least $25 million next season. -- Ben Golliver

Read the full Hornets offseason recap/season preview

Atlanta Hawks: Sept. 3
Key additions: Luguentz Dort, Aaron Wiggins, Kingston Flemings, Devin Carter, Ryan Nembhard, Zuby Ejiofor, Henri Veesaar

Key retentions: CJ McCollum, Jock Landale

Key subtractions: Zaccharie Risacher, Jonathan Kuminga, Gabe Vincent, Keaton Wallace

Atlanta continued to move forward from the Trae Young trade last season by being opportunistic this offseason.

The Hawks acquired Dort and Wiggins in separate trades from the Oklahoma City Thunder to add more help around emerging star Jalen Johnson. The Hawks also kept McCollum on a one-year, $21 million deal and drafted Flemings eighth overall.

Atlanta is loaded with young wings looking to take a step forward under Quin Snyder like Nickeil Alexander-Walker did last season in winning Most Improved Player. -- Ohm Youngmisuk

Read the full Hawks offseason recap/season preview

Orlando Magic: Sept. 4
Key additions: C Nikola Vucevic, G Izaiyah Nelson

Key subtractions: F Moritz Wagner, G Jett Howard

Key retentions: F Jonathan Isaac, G Jevon Carter

The Magic's biggest move this offseason was hiring Sean Sweeney to replace Jamahl Mosley.

Orlando also brought Nikola Vucevic back on a one-year, $3.9 million deal since trading him in 2021 and will use his ability to score and shoot to space the floor for Paolo Banchero, Franz Wagner and Desmond Bane.

The Magic blew a 3-1 lead over top-seeded Detroit in the first round of the playoffs after Wagner went down due to injury and were in desperate need of someone who can get easier baskets and make outside shots. Vucevic should help. Moe Wagner departed for Brooklyn via free agency, separating Franz from his brother for the first time in his pro career. -- Ohm Youngmisuk

Read the full Magic offseason recap/season preview

Pacific Division

Los Angeles Lakers: Aug. 24
Key additions: C Walker Kessler, F Sandro Mamukelashvili, G Quentin Grimes, G Collin Sexton, F Kevon Looney, F Matisse Thybulle, G Cameron Carr

Key retentions: G Austin Reaves

Key subtractions: F LeBron James, C Deandre Ayton, G Marcus Smart, F Rui Hachimura, G Luke Kennard, C Jaxson Hayes

James informed the Lakers he would not be returning for next season on June 30. Two days later, the team transformed the roster, with Doncic squarely as the focal point.

The biggest addition -- literally and figuratively -- is 7-foot-2 center Kessler, acquired in a sign-and-trade deal with the Utah Jazz. L.A. sent two unprotected first-round picks in 2031 and 2033 and pick swaps in 2028 and 2030, not to mention a four-year, $130 million contract, to acquire him.

Mamukelashvili, Grimes, Sexton, Looney and Thybulle also signed with the Lakers, and free agent Ziaire Williams and first-round pick Carr bolster the team's young prospect pool of Adou Thiero, Bronny James and Dalton Knecht.

The most important move, though, came when Reaves, coming off a career season in which he averaged 23.3 points, 4.7 rebounds and 5.5 assists per game, signed a four-year, $180 million extension.

When the dust settled, it was a dramatic roster overhaul in what could prove to be one of the most consequential summers in franchise history, with the team also being sold for the second time in 14 months, this time to venture capitalist Josh Kushner and former Disney CEO Bob Iger, who bought the Lakers from Mark Walter at a $12.5 billion valuation. -- Dave McMenamin

Read the full Lakers offseason recap/season preview

LA Clippers: Aug. 25
Key additions: Rui Hachimura, Keaton Wagler, Brandon Ingram (TBD), Gradey Dick (TBD)

Key retentions: Kobe Sanders, Bradley Beal

Key subtractions: Kawhi Leonard (TBD), Nicolas Batum, Bogdan Bogdanovic, John Collins

What started as a reconfiguration at the trade deadline -- acquiring Darius Garland from Cleveland for James Harden and Bennedict Mathurin from Indiana for Ivica Zubac -- turned into a complete overhaul this summer after the Clippers let Bogdan Bogdanovic, Nicolas Batum and John Collins walk.

Their biggest move, however, was trading Leonard to the Toronto Raptors for Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick and draft picks, but that deal is in limbo pending the investigation into alleged salary cap circumvention by the team relating to Leonard's Aspiration endorsement deal.

In the meantime, LA added Illinois guard Wagler with the No. 5 pick in the draft and signed Hachimura away from the crosstown Lakers with a two-year, $28 million deal. And in a surprise move, Bradley Beal -- after declining his $5.6 million contract option for next season in June to test free agency -- ended up re-signing on a two-year, $13.2 million deal in mid-August to stay with the Clippers. -- Dave McMenamin

Read the full Clippers offseason recap/season preview

Golden State Warriors: Aug. 26
Key additions: Yaxel Lendeborg, Brandon Williams, Georges Niang

Key subtractions: Quinten Post, Pat Spencer

Key retentions: Draymond Green, Al Horford, Kristaps Porzingis, Gary Payton II, De'Anthony Melton

The Warriors opted for flexibility and stability over a larger shake-up around Curry. Their much-publicized recruitment of James never gained much traction.

They brought back their veteran frontcourt trio (Green, Horford, Porzingis), but kept them all on short-term maneuverable contracts. They opted for the fit of Melton over a pursuit of scoring guard Anfernee Simons. Their big addition is Lendeborg, the 23-year-old rookie wing who they will rely upon to be a high-minute, high-impact rotation player immediately.

In the bigger picture, they protected their draft pick cupboard and lined up their books to have an ocean of cap space as they peer a bit deeper into the future while their core ages. -- Anthony Slater

Read the full Warriors offseason recap/season preview

Phoenix Suns: Aug. 27
Key additions: F Miles Bridges, F Koa Peat, G Luke Kennard

Key subtractions: G Grayson Allen, F Royce O'Neale

Key retentions: F Dillon Brooks, G Collin Gillespie, C Mark Williams, G Jordan Goodwin

Phoenix followed up its surprising season with a series of moves to mostly keep its team intact, with some adjustments around the margins.

The Suns re-signed Gillespie (four years, $48 million), Williams (three years, $38 million), Goodwin (three years, $19 million) and Brooks (three years, $73 million) to new deals and made a major splash by trading Allen and O'Neale to the Charlotte Hornets for Bridges. And despite not having a pick until No. 47 in the second round of the 2026 draft, Phoenix was able to acquire Arizona player Peat -- who averaged 14.1 points on 52.8% shooting as a freshman for the Wildcats and was key to their Final Four run. -- Dave McMenamin

Read the full Suns offseason recap/season preview

Sacramento Kings: Aug. 28
Key additions: G Darius Acuff Jr., F Alex Karaban, G Emanuel Sharp

Key subtractions: G DeMar DeRozan, G Russell Westbrook

Key retentions: F Precious Achiuwa

Perry, currently in the organization's power seat, is continuing a steady transition toward the younger core he has drafted. Arkansas guard and No. 7 pick Acuff is the spotlight name on a roster populated with six players in their first two NBA seasons.

But they still have notable high-minute holdovers from the past regime, including Murray, Malik Monk, LaVine and Sabonis. Of those four, Murray appears the most locked-in as a stable member of the team's long-term vision. Perry explored trades for Monk, LaVine and Sabonis over the past year, but didn't value the proposed returns, and the three are expected to open the season in Sacramento. -- Anthony Slater

Read the full Kings offseason recap/season preview

Northwest Division

Portland Trail Blazers: Aug. 17
Key additions: G Ja Morant, F Jeremy Sochan

Key retentions: C Robert Williams III

Key subtractions: F Jerami Grant, F Kris Murray, G Matisse Thybulle

Sadly, the Blazers made far more noise this offseason with their off-court business dealings than anything they did with their roster. New owner Tom Dundon's aggressive cost-cutting measures and ongoing fight for arena financing have distracted from the progress that Portland made on the court last season, when it reached the playoffs for the first time since 2021.

Although the Blazers were the only team that sat out June's draft by not making a pick, they will add two high-profile guards to a rotation that otherwise looks very similar to last season. Lillard, a franchise icon, is back from an Achilles tendon injury that sidelined him for the entire 2025-26 campaign, and Morant, a two-time All-Star, arrived in a trade that sent Grant and Murray to the Memphis Grizzlies. -- Ben Golliver

Read the full Blazers offseason recap/season preview

Utah Jazz: Aug. 18
Key additions: G Darryn Peterson, C Jaxson Hayes, G Josh Okogie

Key retentions: C Jusuf Nurkic

Key subtractions: C Walker Kessler

The Jazz finally got some lottery luck, landing at No. 2 and taking Peterson, a gifted guard who has the potential to emerge as the face of the franchise. The hope was that Peterson would be the final major piece in Utah's rebuild, but that plan featured Kessler as the team's long-term starting center. Instead, the Jazz agreed to a sign-and-trade deal that sent Kessler to the Lakers in exchange for a pair of future first-round picks and two swaps.

The return was widely considered to be great value for Utah, particularly after Kessler's deal (four years, $130 million) pushed beyond the Jazz's comfort zone, but there is now a glaring need in the starting lineup alongside Jackson and Lauri Markkanen in the frontcourt. -- Tim MacMahon

Read the full Jazz offseason recap/season preview

Minnesota Timberwolves: Aug. 19
Key additions: G LaMelo Ball, G Josh Green, G Isaiah Evans

Key subtractions: F Julius Randle, C Naz Reid

Key retentions: G Ayo Dosunmu, G Bones Hyland, G Jaylen Clark

Wolves president of basketball operations Tim Connelly continued to show his aggression, orchestrating a four-team trade with the Brooklyn Nets, Chicago Bulls and Charlotte Hornets that sent out three-time All-Star Randle and the 2023-24 Sixth Man of the Year, Reid, and a future first-round pick to bring in the talented -- but polarizing -- Ball.

That move followed Connelly inking 6-foot-4 guard Dosunmu to a five-year, $112 million extension in June, following his acquisition at the deadline.

Minnesota also re-signed wing Clark and guard Hyland and acquired the 6-foot-6 Evans out of Duke with the No. 33 pick in the draft.

Coach Chris Finch also lost his top lieutenant on the bench, Micah Nori, who left to coach the Portland Trail Blazers. -- Dave McMenamin

Read the full Timberwolves offseason recap/season preview

Oklahoma City Thunder: Aug. 20
Key additions: C Aday Mara, G Bennett Stirtz

Key retentions: G Kenrich Williams, C Isaiah Hartenstein

Key subtractions: G Isaiah Joe, G Aaron Wiggins, G Luguentz Dort

The extensions for both Jalen Williams and Chet Holmgren triggered in July, leading to a trio of financially motivated trades to slash the tax bill and cost-control the current roster.

They sent Isaiah Joe to Detroit and traded Aaron Wiggins and Lu Dort to Atlanta in separate moves, eroding their depth.

General manager Sam Presti made clear in an interview with The Oklahoman that the impression he's been given from ownership is "the savings generated this summer, and from being out of the tax the last several years, will be re-allocated to future teams."

That would mean extra breathing room to eventually extend core young players such as Cason Wallace and Ajay Mitchell. Wallace, the likely replacement starter for Dort, is extension eligible off his rookie contract into October. -- Anthony Slater

Read the full Thunder offseason recap/season preview

Denver Nuggets: Aug. 21
Key additions: Marvin Bagley III, Lonnie Walker IV

Key retentions: Spencer Jones, Tyus Jones

Key subtractions: Watson, Tim Hardaway Jr., Jonas Valanciunas

Finding a resolution to Watson's restricted free agency was Denver's most important piece of summer business.

Watson is a draft success story, rising from the 30th overall pick into one of the league's more intriguing young two-way wings. But retaining the 23-year-old would have been expensive -- via either a sky-high luxury tax bill or a salary-slashing move to get off an important veteran and generate more breathing room for a new deal.

After Wednesday's deal to send Watson to Cleveland, Denver's front office can shift its attention to escaping the salary cap's second apron. The Nuggets are currently the league's only team above it. -- Anthony Slater

Southwest Division

Memphis Grizzlies: Aug. 14
Key additions: F Cameron Boozer, G D'Angelo Russell, F Isaiah Stewart, F Jerami Grant, F Kris Murray, C Quinten Post

Key retentions: None

Key subtractions: G Ja Morant, F Santi Aldama

Memphis finally traded Ja Morant, turning the last page from an ultimately disappointing chapter in franchise history, and already has his replacement as the face of the franchise in place: No. 3 pick Cameron Boozer. GM Zach Kleiman has overhauled the roster in the past few transaction cycles, acquiring four first-round picks when he traded Desmond Bane, a few more when he dealt Jaren Jackson Jr. and none for Morant, whose departure signaled a fresh start for the Grizzlies and him.

Memphis is in a full-blown youth movement, as 21-year-old forward GG Jackson is now the longest-tenured player on the roster. The Grizzlies say they believe they have a long-term foundation in place with their last few lottery picks: center Zach Edey, small forward Cedric Coward and power forward Boozer. -- Tim MacMahon

Read the full Grizzlies offseason recap/season preview

New Orleans Pelicans: Aug. 13
Key additions: None

Key retentions: C DeAndre Jordan

Key subtractions: F Kevon Looney

Despite capturing a combined 47 wins over the last two seasons under executive vice president Joe Dumars and general manager Troy Weaver, the Pelicans clearly believe that internal growth is the best path forward. Perhaps that justifies a near-silent summer in which the hiring of new coach Jamahl Mosley turned out to be the team's most notable move. Mosley becomes New Orleans' third coach since Dumars took the helm in April 2025. In addition to drafting Jaron Pierre Jr. in the second round, New Orleans signed just two new players over the summer in Kobe Bufkin and Hunter Dickinson, while bringing back 14 of the 15 players from last season's squad. -- Michael C. Wright

Dallas Mavericks: Aug. 12
Key additions: F Morez Johnson Jr., F Zaccharie Risacher

Key retentions: Moussa Cisse

Key subtractions: Khris Middleton, Ryan Nembhard

The major changes made by the Mavericks this offseason were in the managerial and coaching ranks. After a seasonlong search, team governor Patrick Dumont hired Masai Ujiri to run the franchise's basketball operations, bringing the architect of the Toronto Raptors' 2019 title team to Dallas. Ujiri decided to part ways with coach Jason Kidd and recruited Dusty May, fresh off an NCAA title with Michigan, to replace him.

Johnson, who played for May at Michigan before the Mavs selected him with the No. 9 pick in the draft, is the headliner of the additions to the roster. Dallas added three potential immediate contributors in a six-team deal, acquiring former Grizzlies forward Santi Aldama, ex-Pistons guard Marcus Sasser and EuroLeague veteran Tarik Biberovic. The franchise also landed former No. 1 pick as part of the trade that sent Luguentz Dort from the Oklahoma City Thunder to the Atlanta Hawks. -- MacMahon

Key additions: G Marcus Smart, G Bogdan Bogdanovic

Key retentions: F Tari Eason

Key subtractions: F Dorian Finney-Smith, G Josh Okogie

After suffering a first-round postseason exit for the second consecutive season, the Rockets resisted the temptation to jump into the Giannis Antetokounmpo sweepstakes after adding former MVP Durant last summer. General manager Rafael Stone and coach Ime Udoka will instead lean on growth from the team's collection of young talent acquired in recent years, not to mention the continuity that comes with those players developing together over multiple seasons.

Houston signed Tari Eason to a five-year, $81.5 million extension over the summer. But outside of that, the Rockets focused on bolstering depth by bringing aboard veterans Marcus Smart and Bogdan Bogdanovic. The club also brought in renowned shooting coach Chip Engelland from Oklahoma City. Engelland spent more than a decade with the San Antonio Spurs, winning two titles. -- Wright

Key additions: F Tobias Harris

San Antonio's surprising run to the NBA Finals never obscured its long-term vision for building a sustainable competitor around Victor Wembanyama. Clearly, the Frenchman views the future similarly, considering he signed a 25% max extension worth $252 million instead of the available 30% supermax escalators that would've rocketed the contract to $303 million.

Wembanyama did it to keep San Antonio's talented young core together for as long as possible, with added flexibility to acquire needed supporting players. The Spurs grabbed one of those in free agency in Harris, an experienced, reliable scorer who adds size (6-foot-8, 226 pounds) and physicality on defense while bolstering frontcourt depth in the draft. -- Wright

stories.headline: Max vs 100: Verstappen jokes taking on '200' drivers next time after winning crazy challenge
stories.summary: Max Verstappen has joked that he's ready to race 200 drivers next after storming from the back of a 101-grid to take victory in his half his allotted time in Max vs 100 on Wednesday.
stories.body:
Max Verstappen has joked that he's ready to race 200 drivers next after storming from the back of a 101-grid to take victory in his half his allotted time in Max vs 100 on Wednesday.

Verstappen needed just 14 laps, and 35 minutes, to complete the challenge, which was broadcast live globally on ESPN on Disney+.

The unique go-karting race represented the latest of the four-time world champions' side quests away from Formula 1 and the Red Bull driver is already looking ahead to his next test.

"Yeah, that's what I said before ... I was like maybe 200 [drivers] and then we'll see again," he told the media after the race at Silverstone.

The event took place on a custom-built track, a mix of two different circuits: 1.3km of permanent karting track on the Silverstone infield, with another 1.15km of temporary track added specifically for this event.

He was given 30 laps, or 75 minutes, to get the job done against athletes, content creators, journalists and other celebrities, and he ended up exceeding everyone's expectations, including his own.

Verstappen managed to pass 63 drivers on the very first lap and when he was asked if he had a strategy heading into the race, he said: "I mean, when I was walking to the grid and I saw where I had to start it's like oof, that's a very far way back. But after my first lap I was like I think we're all right, I think we're good.

"It was mainly just depending on the first two laps, that's why I was like OK if I clear the first two laps, what can it be like at 15-20 laps. But yeah, I think the first lap went a bit better than expected, so that helps a lot.

- Max Verstappen wins Max vs 100 in style after overtaking 100 go-karters in 35 minutes

- Max vs 100: Highlights, commentary as Verstappen beats 100 go-karters - as it happened

- Max vs 100: How Verstappen's karting years made an F1 champion - and prepared him for an all-new test

"The first lap is just chaos so you just want to survive and then after that it's a bit like you're just hunting them down. So that's also quite nice where you have to just put the laps in by yourself and you catch them one by one.

"You just act on instinct, whatever happens when the lights go out, you kind of just see where the gaps are and then you also kind of need to trust the few people around you that they don't do anything crazy. But to be honest, they didn't."

He managed to clear the field but he spent several laps catching the top three -- journalist Jacky Martens, YouTuber Zac Alsop and Red Bull's own Lewis Osler.

Verstappen has always had fond memories of his karting days, and heading into the event he said the last time he raced in a "proper go-kart" was 2016.

"It's just great that with Red Bull they always come up with some crazy fun things and it suits me as well," he said.

"I can really be myself and I think also the way it was organised today, I know that it requires a lot of effort to be able to do something like this."

stories.headline: Messi nets 100th Miami goal en route to Campeones Cup win
stories.summary: Lionel Messi scored his 100th goal for Inter Miami in all competitions after heading home the opener in a 2-0 win over Cruz Azul in the Campeones Cup on Wednesday night at Nu Stadium.
stories.body:
MIAMI -- Lionel Messi scored his 100th goal for Inter Miami in all competitions after heading home the opener in a 2-0 win over Cruz Azul in the Campeones Cup on Wednesday night at Nu Stadium.

Messi's goal put Miami up 1-0 in the annual match between the champion of MLS and Liga MX before a late header from Casemiro put the game away to hand new coach Cristian "Kily" González a trophy in his first match in charge.

"Leo [Messi] told me I was going to become a champion, and he made it happen," González said.

"Moving forward, this gives us a huge morale boost, it's a vital element for us, and while we've achieved this, we have to keep going."

Luis Suárez set up the opener in the 24th minute with a perfectly lofted cross from the right side that Messi ran onto, outjumping his marker and scoring a rare goal with his head.

González led his first training session with Inter Miami on Tuesday after landing in Miami from Argentina earlier in the morning. The team had reached an agreement with González to replace interim coach Guillermo Hoyos on Aug. 27, but he was unable to take over until receiving his work permit.

His first game as Miami coach will be one to remember with Messi scoring his 100th goal for the club and the team picking up a trophy on the night.

"It's become a normality [for Messi] but it isn't," Rodrigo de Paul said about his Miami teammate.

"We have to enjoy him, admire him, see him with the love that he plays each game. Luckily, I've had him by my side for many years. I try to enjoy him to the maximum."

Messi, a World Cup winner in 2022, reached the milestone in only 115 games for Inter Miami, marking the quickest he has recorded 100 goals for any team he has represented. Messi previously reached the mark with Barcelona in 188 games and 174 games with Argentina.

Since joining Miami in 2023, Messi has 76 goals in MLS, 14 in Leagues Cup action, eight in the Concacaf Champions Cup and one at the FIFA Club World Cup.

Messi made an instant impact in south Florida since signing with Miami, leading the Herons to the 2023 Leagues Cup title just weeks after marking his debut against Cruz Azul -- the team against which he scored his first Miami goal.

The Inter Miami captain also guided the team to the 2024 Supporters' Shield -- setting the record for most points (74) in an MLS season -- and starred in the playoffs during a run to the 2025 MLS Cup title last year.

Messi has now scored 929 goals for club and country during his career and leads MLS with 19 goals in 22 games so far this season.

stories.headline: Borussia Dortmund teenager Konstantinos Karetsas returns to training after Champions League health scare
stories.summary: Borussia Dortmund says 18-year-old midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas is back in training just over a week after he slumped to the ground in an alarming medical incident on his Champions League debut.
stories.body:
Borussia Dortmund have said 18-year-old midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas is back in training just over a week after he slumped to the ground in an alarming medical incident on his Champions League debut.

Karetsas passed the ball to a teammate then signaled his distress to the referee before sitting on the grass during Dortmund's 3-2 win over Villarreal on Sept. 8.

He was in tears as he was stretchered off with suspected circulatory problems and was then taken to a hospital, where he stayed for much of last week.

"Konstantinos Karetsas is back in team training as of Wednesday after doing individual sessions at the start of the week," Dortmund said. "It was his first joint session with his teammates after he was taken off with circulatory problems in the game against Villarreal."

Dortmund hasn't specified the nature of any diagnosis for Karetsas, who was signed from Genk for a reported fee of $34.6 million last month, and didn't indicate whether he would be able to play Saturday against Stuttgart in the Bundesliga.

Karetsas plays internationally for Greece but was born in Belgium, where local media have reported that dehydration was suspected as a factor.

"I'm doing really well," he said in a video recorded during a visit to his old club Genk and published Monday on X. "We tested everything and everything is fine. I just need to adjust a bit to the intensity but that will come with time."

"I went out with him but in that moment, he wasn't able to speak," Book said.
