Karetsas was able to cheer on his teammates from the stands in Saturday's 3-0 win over Paderborn.

Managing director Lars Ricken said there had been "no warning signs" of any circulatory problems prior to the incident.

stories.headline: Alexa Grasso shows off flyweight's elite status in women's P4P top 10
stories.summary: Former UFC champion puts elite status of women's flyweight division on display in ESPN's P4P top 10.
stories.body:
It's uncommon for two fighters ranked in the pound-for-pound top 10 to meet in a bout with no championship at stake. But that was the case at Saturday's fourth annual Noche UFC, where Alexa Grasso faced Manon Fiorot.

Grasso is a former women's flyweight champion and Fiorot competed for the belt last year, so their status as MMA elites was well established before they fought. And when Grasso won by unanimous decision, she further solidified her standing in the ESPN women's pound-for-pound rankings.

The top five of the rankings remains intact, and Grasso moves up from 10th to replace Fiorot at No. 6. Fiorot slips two positions to No. 8 in a pound-for-pound hierarchy in which seven of the 10 ranked women compete at flyweight (including Zhang Weili, the former UFC strawweight champion who last fought in an unsuccessful challenge of Valentina Shevchenko in November).

With Shevchenko injured and having vacated her title, there will be much scrambling for the top spot, which will be at stake when No. 5 Natalia Silva fights unranked Wang Cong on Oct. 3.

For the ESPN divisional MMA rankings, click here.

Note: Results are current; rankings are as of Sept. 16. To be eligible for the rankings, a fighter must have competed over the past 12 months or must have an upcoming fight booked. Fighters who have been dropped for inactivity can be reinstated only after they compete.

Women's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Valentina Shevchenko

UFC flyweight

Record: 26-4-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Zhang Weili, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

Shevchenko's dominance came under question in 2022 and 2023, when she went 1-1-1 in a trilogy with Alexa Grasso. Boy, does that feel like a long time ago now. Shevchenko more than reasserted herself as the best flyweight in the world, and then she established herself as the No. 1 woman in the world, period. It wasn't surprising that she beat Zhang, but it was surprising how easy she made it look. Shevchenko is out injured, however, so she has vacated her UFC title, which will be up for grabs when Natalia Silva meets Wang Cong on Oct. 3.

2. Zhang Weili

UFC flyweight / strawweight

Record: 26-4

Last: L (UD) vs. Valentina Shevchenko, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

It's hard to move up in weight, especially at the highest level. That sounds like it should be obvious, but Zhang had been dominant at 115 pounds for so long, some of us might have taken for granted how big of a challenge moving to 125 would be. UFC 322 was a bad night for Zhang, but she doesn't have many. And if she decides to stay at flyweight, it certainly seems reasonable to believe she'll fare better in the future.

3. Cris Cyborg

PFL featherweight champion

Record: 30-2, 1 NC

Last: W (UD) vs. Ketlen Vieira, Aug. 22

Next: TBA

It had been a while since Cyborg had fought an elite opponent in MMA until she met Larissa Pacheco in 2024. That was a legitimate matchup -- and many within the industry were predicting Cyborg's downfall. Instead, she took out the PFL's two-weight champion, upending all of Pacheco's momentum. One of the original pioneers of women's MMA is once again a champion after getting her second career submission at PFL Lyon in December. The PFL promoted her fight with Vieira as a retirement bout, but after her win Cyborg did not sound like someone who is done fighting.

4. Mackenzie Dern

UFC strawweight champion

Record: 17-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Gillian Robertson, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Dern's rise to the 115-pound throne was truly a changing of the guard. She is the division's first first-time champion since 2019, because the previous three champs -- Zhang Weili, Carla Esparza and Rose Namajunas -- all were in their second reigns. Dern, nearly a decade into her MMA career after multiple jiu-jitsu world championships, has won four fights in a row, including a dominant performance against a fellow grappling-heavy fighter, Robertson, in her first title defense.

5. Natalia Silva

UFC flyweight

Record: 20-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Rose Namajunas, Jan. 24

Next: Oct. 3 vs. Wang Cong

Silva is looking every bit the part of a future UFC champion following a dominant display against Alexa Grasso at UFC 315 and a victory over Namajunas at UFC 324. Silva's stick-and-move style has frustrated even the highest level of opponent, and she's got youth on her side as she won't turn 30 until 2027. With an injured Valentina Shevchenko having vacated the title, Silva will fight Wang for the belt at UFC 332.

6. Alexa Grasso

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 10

Record: 18-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Manon Fiorot, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Grasso went nearly three years without winning a fight, but her 2023 win right before the skid was a huge one, a submission of Valentina Shevchenko for the UFC title. What followed were two more fights with Shevchenko -- a draw, then a loss -- and then a loss to Natalia Silva. But she reasserted herself with a finish of Maycee Barber in March, then got the best of Fiorot, a fellow title contender, at Noche UFC to put herself in position for another title shot.

7. Dakota Ditcheva

PFL flyweight

Record: 16-0

Last: W (UD) vs. Denise Kielholtz, July 31

Next: TBA

Not only did Ditcheva win the PFL's flyweight season in 2024, but she did so in spectacular fashion -- a TKO finish over Taila Santos, who once challenged for a UFC title. Ditcheva fought only once in 2025, dominating Sumiko Inaba in the co-main event of the first PFL Champions Series card in Cape Town, South Africa. She then spent over a year on the sideline, healing injuries to both hands, before returning at PFL New York with a dominant win over Kielholtz.

8. Manon Fiorot

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 6

Record: 13-3

Last: L (UD) vs. Alexa Grasso, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Fiorot had handled everyone the UFC put in front of her -- except the champion, Valentina Shevchenko, who defeated the Frenchwoman at UFC 315 in May 2025. But then, with another title shot within her grasp, Fiorot ran into Grasso, a former champion, at Noche UFC and lost a competitive fight.

9. Erin Blanchfield

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 8

Record: 14-2

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Tracy Cortez, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: Oct. 17 vs. Jasmine Jasudavicius

Her rise toward the top of the division was derailed by a March 2024 loss to Manon Fiorot, but Blanchfield bounced back with two straight wins, including one over two-time former strawweight champion Rose Namajunas in November 2024. If she wins her October bout with Jasudavicius, a fellow top-10 flyweight contender, Blanchfield would inch ever closer to a title shot.

10. Tatiana Suarez

UFC strawweight

Previous ranking: 9

Record: 12-1

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Loopy Godínez, April 11

Next: TBA

If Suarez is still feeling the effects of last year's humbling defeat to Zhang Weili in a title challenge, she certainly didn't show it at UFC 327, overcoming early adversity to thrash Godinez, a fellow top-10 strawweight. Suarez is going to be a tough out for anyone at 115 pounds.

How our panel voted
Brett Okamoto: 1. Valentina Shevchenko; 2. Zhang Weili; 3. Mackenzie Dern; 4. Cris Cyborg; 5. Alexa Grasso; 6. Manon Fiorot; 7. Dakota Ditcheva; 8. Natalia Silva; 9. Erin Blanchfield; 10. Tatiana Suarez.

Carlos Contreras Legaspi: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Cyborg; 3. Zhang; 4. Dern; 5. Silva; 6. Grasso; 7. Ditcheva; 8. Suarez; 9. Fiorot; 10. Blanchfield.

Andrew Davis: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Zhang; 3. Cyborg; 4. Dern; 5. Silva; 6. Grasso; 7. Blanchfield; 8. Ditcheva; 9. Suarez; 10. Fiorot.

Dre Waters: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Zhang; 3. Cyborg; 4. Silva; 5. Dern; 6. Grasso; 7. Ditcheva; 8. Blanchfield; 9. Fiorot; 10. Suarez.

Jeff Wagenheim: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Zhang; 3. Cyborg; 4. Silva; 5. Grasso; 6. Dern; 7. Fiorot; 8. Blanchfield; 9. Suarez; 10. Ditcheva.

Men's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Islam Makhachev

UFC welterweight champion

Record: 29-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Ian Machado Garry, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Makhachev vacated the UFC lightweight championship to go for a second title at welterweight. By winning that belt last November with a thrashing of Jack Della Maddalena, Makhachev staked his place among MMA's greatest -- not just in today's sport but of all time. His win over Machado Garry at UFC 330 was his 17th straight, breaking the UFC record for consecutive wins. Makhachev is piling up unprecedented achievements.

2. Petr Yan

UFC bantamweight champion

Record: 20-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Merab Dvalishvili, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Dvalishvili

What a return to the top it's been for Yan. He began his career with 15 consecutive wins before going on a 1-4 run from 2021 to 2023. That almost doesn't feel real now, after watching him reclaim his throne against Dvalishvili, who once handed him the worst loss of his career. Yan took a major detour, but this was the destination we felt he was capable of before the skid. He once again looks like one of the best fighters on the planet. He can prove it by beating Dvalishvili again.

3. Merab Dvalishvili

UFC bantamweight

Record: 21-5

Last: L (UD) vs. Petr Yan, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Yan

Dvalishvili was on one of the most impressive runs through the UFC's bantamweight division ever. Not only did he defeat Sean O'Malley for the second time in nine months at UFC 316, but he showcased a new part of his game, finishing O'Malley with a guillotine. Starting in August 2022, Dvalishvili beat José Aldo, Yan, Henry Cejudo, O'Malley (twice), Umar Nurmagomedov and Cory Sandhagen. But at UFC 323, in an attempt to become the first champion in UFC history to successfully defend a title four times in a calendar year, Dvalishvili lost a rematch with Yan. They will fight for a third time at UFC 333.

4. Tom Aspinall

UFC heavyweight

Record: 15-3, 1 NC

Last: NC1 vs. Ciryl Gane, Oct. 25, 2025

Next: TBA

You can make a case that Aspinall is the most dynamic, skillful, talented heavyweight the sport has seen. He is dominating opponents in a way that is unmatched. No one can last a round with him. He had hoped to prove his supremacy against Jon Jones, but Jones opted to retire, elevating Aspinall from interim champion. His first defense of the undisputed belt ended anticlimactically, as an eye poke resulted in his UFC 321 fight with Gane being declared a no-contest. Still recovering from the eye injury, Aspinall vacated his title on Sept. 14.

5. Ilia Topuria

UFC lightweight

Record: 17-1

Last: L (TKO4) vs. Justin Gaethje, June 14

Next: TBA

Topuria was an undefeated two-division champion when he ran into Gaethje at UFC Freedom 250 and was brutalized in a stoppage loss. How will that affect the immediate future of Topuria? His knockout wins over two of the greatest featherweights, Alexander Volkanovski and Max Holloway, gave him an intimidating aura. Can the former champion get that back?

6. Justin Gaethje

UFC lightweight champion

Record: 28-5

Last: W (TKO4) vs. Ilia Topuria, June 14

Next: TBA

Gaethje has spent his 15-year career thrilling MMA fans, but before the title bout on the White House lawn, all he had to show for it -- aside from 15 bonus checks in 15 UFC appearances -- were two missed opportunities to be an undisputed champion. His fourth-round TKO of Topuria got Gaethje over the hump. It was a resilient performance in a back-and-forth battle that is a prime candidate for fight of the year. More important for Gaethje: At age 37, he is finally sitting at the top of the mountain.

7. Alexander Volkanovski

UFC featherweight champion

Record: 28-4

Last: W (UD) vs. Diego Lopes, Jan. 31

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Movsar Evloev

It felt as if the sport had started to write Volkanovski's eulogy following his knockout loss to Ilia Topuria in February 2024. Volkanovski noticed and made a point of proving to everyone he still has plenty left by recapturing the featherweight belt at UFC 314, the first of two consecutive wins over Lopes. His age (37) will likely continue to be a prefight topic, which is fine because Volkanovski enjoys proving people wrong. Can he hand Evloev his first loss at UFC 333?

8. Alexandre Pantoja

UFC flyweight

Record: 30-6

Last: L (TKO1) vs. Joshua Van, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Sept. 19 vs. Joshua Van

Pantoja became the UFC's unquestioned flyweight king by racking up four title defenses, including two in pay-per-view main events in 2024. He built his winning streak to eight in his UFC 317 win over Kai Kara-France, whom he had already defeated before, like other challengers. But he lost his belt in a gruesome way, injuring his elbow in the opening seconds of a UFC 323 fight with Van. Pantoja gets his rematch with Van at UFC 331.

9. Ciryl Gane

UFC heavyweight interim champion

Record: 14-2, 1 NC

Last: W (TKO2) vs. Alex Pereira, June 14

Next: TBA

Gane is unique in that he is the first -- and could very well go down as the only -- heavyweight to face the division's four biggest names in Francis Ngannou, Jon Jones, Tom Aspinall and Pereira. None of those four have fought each other, yet all four have have fought the Frenchman. Gane was 0-2 with a no-contest against that group before he knocked out Pereira in the second round of their interim title fight. Gane was heralded as the future of the generation when he broke onto the scene, but endured growing pains in losses to Ngannou and Jones. He looks formidable now, and no one will be counting him out if he faces Aspinall in a title unification bout.

10. Alex Pereira

UFC heavyweight / light heavyweight

Record: 13-4

Last: L (TKO2) vs. Ciryl Gane, June 14

Next: TBA

He was on the verge of making history when the opportunity fell apart. Pereira was a UFC champion at middleweight, then light heavyweight, but his unprecedented pursuit of a belt in a third weight class did not go well for the Brazilian, who lost an interim heavyweight title fight to Gane on the White House card. At 39 years old, Pereira does not have much time left to recapture the magic.

Other fighters receiving votes: Joshua Van and Arman Tsarukyan.

stories.headline: NRL Midweek Mail semifinals: Bulldogs move to lock away rising rookie
stories.summary: Ronaldo Mulitalo is determined to honour his departing Sharks teammates, Sione Katoa has opened up about his future at the Cowboys and his finals days at the Sharks, while Nathan Cleary is fighting the clock to be fit for Penrith's prelim.
stories.body:
The NRL rarely stands still.

Between training sessions, media appearances, and behind-the-scenes conversations, new storylines often begin to emerge before the weekend arrives.

Throughout the week, ESPN will be gathering notes, insights, and updates from around the competition heading into the NRL's semifinal week.

Bulldogs move early to lock down rising forward

The Bulldogs have moved early to lock down rising forward Alekolasimi 'AJ' Jones, with the club's Rookie of the Year agreeing to a two-year contract extension.

ESPN understands Jones, who was already contracted through the 2027 season, has agreed to a new deal that will keep him at Belmore beyond his existing contract.

The move ensures Jones' future is secured before he would have been free to negotiate with rival clubs for 2028 from November 1.

Kennedy backs Hynes amid criticism

Will Kennedy believes Nicho Hynes has grown from the criticism that has followed him throughout his career, praising the Sharks star ahead of their semi-final against the Roosters.

"He's learned a lot from all the criticism he gets and he's taken a step forward," Kennedy said. "For me, I just want to get around him because he's my brother and I want to play next to him."

Trindall 'really good' after shoulder scare

Will Kennedy says Braydon Trindall has pulled up well after battling through a shoulder issue in Cronulla's finals win over North Queensland.

Kennedy said Trindall had been "really dialled in on the mental side" of his game and indicated the halfback had told him he was feeling "really good" ahead of the Roosters clash.

Mulitalo relishing 'Marky Mark' rematch

Ronaldo Mulitalo is embracing another blockbuster battle with Roosters star Mark Nawaqanitawase, describing the departing winger as a "generational talent".

Mulitalo said Nawaqanitawase "brings the best out of me" and revealed their on-field rivalry is largely one-sided when it comes to the verbal exchanges.

"He's a gentleman out there... he doesn't really say anything. I think it's more myself," Mulitalo joked. "He knows I'm just going to keep talking, so he just ignores me anyway."

Mulitalo determined to honour departing Sharks

Ronaldo Mulitalo says Cronulla's finals run carries added significance with several longtime teammates set to leave the club at season's end.

Mulitalo said he has played alongside some of the departing Sharks since he was 16 and wants to "honour those boys" with his performance against the Roosters.

"I don't want to let them down and disappoint them, winning the game is the most important part of the week for me."

Katoa reveals Cowboys appeal

Sione Katoa has revealed North Queensland's attacking style was a major attraction behind his move to the Cowboys in 2027.

After helping eliminate his future club from the finals, Katoa told ESPN he "loves the style of footy" they play, describing it as "free footy" and similar to Cronulla's attack.

Katoa emotional over Sharks farewell
He also admitted the reality that every game could be his last for Cronulla is beginning to sink in.

"Tonight might have been the last week, maybe the last game," he told ESPN after scoring a double against North Queensland.

"I'm very happy right now that I get another week with my brothers and play again."

Cleary racing clock for preliminary final

Nathan Cleary is in doubt for Penrith's preliminary final after scans revealed an stress-related bone issue in his foot.

The Panthers will assess and monitor their star halfback over the next fortnight, with their week off providing valuable recovery time.

Cleary has, however, been cleared of any suspension concern after receiving only a Grade 1 Dangerous Contact charge for his incident with Hugo Savala.

stories.body:
Coventry boss Frank Lampard has urged his players to stay positive ahead of Saturday's Premier League trip to Nottingham Forest.

The Sky Blues have lost all four of their top-flight games so far without scoring a goal, and also crashed out of the Carabao Cup to Aston Villa on Wednesday.

Lampard told a news conference: "We just have to [stay positive] because it is football. We have been privileged for a while to win a lot of football matches here.

"It is more difficult when you don't -- that makes the job of all of us tougher because that is what we are here for and what you want to do.

"Sometimes it is human nature to feel down but we have just got to focus on the work that we have got to do to keep trying to improve and to get results."

Lampard has selection problems ahead of the trip to the City Ground with his main striker Taiwo Awoniyi suspended and defender Aurèle Amenda facing time on the sidelines with a suspected calf injury.

With a number of experienced players still some weeks away from regaining fitness, Lampard welcomed the impending international break as an opportunity to restore his side to full strength ahead of the return to league action.

Lampard, who revealed a behind-closed-doors game has been arranged during the period, added: "It's just one we will manage physically but I think the opportunity to get players fit is a good thing for us."

stories.headline: NHL rookie watch list: The next wave of young hockey superstars
stories.summary: These are the top first-year players to monitor for 2026-27. Who will break out first?
stories.body:
NHL training camps are getting underway, and the new wave of rookies expected to play impactful roles is very notable. Three of the top 10 picks from the 2026 draft could see significant NHL time this season.

And for the first time in a while, a goaltender makes an appearance on a preseason watch list. Add in a few players who signed at the conclusion of the 2025-26 NCAA season and there is more than enough talent for an intriguing Calder Trophy race.

Here are 10 first-year players to monitor as the 2026-27 season begins:

Note: Ages are as of opening night, Sept. 29.

Gavin McKenna, LW, Toronto Maple Leafs
Age: 18 | Draft: 2026 No. 1

McKenna was going to be in the spotlight regardless of where he landed. The moment the Maple Leafs won the draft lottery, the spotlight cranked to 11.

McKenna will slot into a top six in Toronto that has Auston Matthews, William Nylander, John Tavares and Matthew Knies. Regardless of which line he plays on, he's going to have the opportunity to create offense with elite talent. Whether he gets first- or second-unit power-play opportunities remains to be seen, but he's going to get time on one of them.

How he adjusts to NHL pace and physicality will ultimately determine how successful his rookie season is. If he meshes well and becomes a primary setup man for Matthews and Knies, 65-plus points is not out of the question. That would likely mean a much-needed rebound season from Matthews, further elevating McKenna's importance to Toronto's immediate future.

McKenna is going to be under the microscope more than any other rookie this season. If he plays well, Toronto will get the offensive jolt that has been missing.

Porter Martone, RW, Philadelphia Flyers
Age: 19 | Draft: 2025 No. 6

If his first cup of coffee in the NHL was any indication, Martone should probably start the season as the Calder favorite. Not only was he excellent for the Flyers in the stretch run, but he was vital in the Flyers' playoff series against the Penguins. The big winger has already endeared himself to the Flyers faithful and more importantly, head coach Ron Hextall.

Playing a consistent top-six role with extended time on the top power-play unit will give Martone plenty of opportunity to pile up the points. Philadelphia was not the most entertaining team to watch last season, given their focus on defense and lack of offensive firepower. Martone was an immediate offensive catalyst and gave the Flyers a dimension they were missing.

He's going to be one of their most important players in the present and future, especially if the Flyers want to avoid a step back this season. Whether he is scoring, creating offense or agitating opponents, the perfect Philadelphia Flyer is going to be an impactful rookie and extremely fun to watch.

Ivar Stenberg, LW, San Jose Sharks
Age: 18 | Draft: 2026 No. 2

The second overall pick joins a Sharks team that seems primed to take a major step forward. The Sharks, like the Leafs, jumped from further back (ninth) to second via the lottery, and drafted Stenberg with the pick. Many scouts believed Stenberg was the most NHL-ready of the top prospects and that his professional experience in Sweden would serve him well in a middle-six role during his rookie season.

Stenberg is a tremendous talent, who is capable of impacting the game both offensively and defensively. Should he play his way onto Macklin Celebrini or Michael Misa's wing, there is a real opportunity for him to produce offensively. Regardless of where he plays, Stenberg is likely to have the best two-way impact of the entire rookie crop. Stenberg's combination of two-way play and offensive play-driving ability should be a major boost for the Sharks and may help put them over the top as a wild-card team this season.

If Stenberg finds himself in the top six, producing offensively, and playing secondary matchups, he's going to be in the conversation for the Calder. He is exactly the type of forward who can slot in with San Jose's young crop of elite skill and elevate their play.

James Hagens, C, Boston Bruins
Age: 19 | Draft: 2025 No. 7

The Bruins couldn't believe when the top-line center from Boston College was sitting there for them at No. 7 in 2025. Fast-forward to now, and Hagens was far and away the best player at B's rookie camp and has a real shot to make the Bruins in 2026.

He's one to watch because the Bruins are already a decent team and there is no need to rush him. Having said that, Hagens' raw offensive talent is greater than any other option Boston has in the middle of the ice. His shot has come a long way, making Hagens a true scoring threat and an even more dangerous dual-threat attacker.

There is a distinct possibility that Hagens breaks camp on the wing with the Bruins, simply because the Bruins believe it is better for his development to play in the NHL rather than the AHL. He would certainly jolt the Bruins' offense and give it a dimension it has lacked the past couple of years. Hagens has true potential to be a top-line center and the ability to produce 55-plus points in a top-six role in his rookie season.

Cole Hutson, D, Washington Capitals
Age: 20 | Draft: 2024 No. 43

With John Carlson gone, Hutson is going to get elevated offensive opportunities in his first full NHL season. He's likely to quarterback the second power-play unit which should feature Jordan Kyrou and fellow rookie Ilya Protas.

In a 14-game audition with the Capitals last season, Hutson notched 10 points and generally impressed. He consistently showed excellent skating ability, moving laterally with ease, changing gears in tight areas and facilitating offense. His first pass is going to drive a ton of transition offense, and his in-zone offense is going to create scoring chances with regularity.

Hutson's ability to create space with his skating, find passing lanes and thread pucks through coverage should make him the premier rookie defender in the class. He will likely start in sheltered minutes given the talent ahead of him on the depth chart while being given opportunities to earn more ice time as the season progresses.

Ilya Protas, LW, Washington Capitals
Age: 20 | Draft: 2024 No. 75

The second Capitals rookie to watch is another familiar name. Ilya Protas is the younger brother of Aliaksei, who is a mainstay in Washington's top six. The younger Protas has a similar build to his brother, and he won AHL Rookie of the year in 2025-26 after averaging more than two points per game in the OHL in 2024-25 as an 18-year-old.

After a nearly point-per-game AHL season, Protas is primed for a shot with the big club. There is depth ahead of him, but he should be given a chance to play a bottom-six role. His versatility may see him start on the wing, but with the injury history to the Capitals' centers, he is likely to get an opportunity there at some point.

Protas is the epitome of the young player that contenders need on an entry-level contract to take advantage of playing in the bottom six. There is every reason to believe the younger Protas will produce offensively against softer matchups and a 40-point season should be attainable.

Longer term, the Capitals expect the younger Protas to be a key piece of their powerful top six that already features Tom Wilson, Alex Tuch and Ilya's older brother.

Anton Frondell, C, Chicago Blackhawks
Age: 19 | Draft: 2025 No. 3

The third overall pick in 2025 looked every bit the part of an NHL top-six player in his 12-game audition to end last season.

Frondell is a foundational piece of Chicago's future, one who needs to start moving in the right direction. With Connor Bedard out to start the season, Frondell is going to have the opportunity to play big minutes in key situations from the outset.

His dual-threat offensive game, combined with ability to drive play should allow him to produce offensively and keep the puck out of Chicago's end. If he gets top power-play minutes throughout the season and retains a top-six role upon Bedard's return, it's quite possible he scores 65 points in a full season. If Chicago takes a step toward playoff contention this season, Frondell could be a major reason why -- and that will boost his Calder candidacy.

Roman Kantserov, RW, Chicago Blackhawks
Age: 22 | Draft: 2023 No. 44

One of the most intriguing rookies is likely to start in the season in Chicago's top six. Kantserov is coming off a point per game season in the KHL as a 21-year-old and has the skating and playmaking ability to be a real offensive threat in the NHL.

He's lesser known largely due to lack of coverage in the Russian leagues, making him the player most likely to surprise NHL fans seeing him for the first time. His quick puck-moving ability combined with chance generation off the rush will fit will with the type of offense Chicago's young players are trying to create.

There is always an adjustment period for players from overseas, and it would not be surprising if it took him a month or two to adjust. However, players with this skill set almost always have a measurable impact in their rookie season, and Kantserov should be no different. A 45-point campaign would be a wonderful success as Kantserov adjusts to the NHL and earns more offensive opportunities.

Viggo Bjorck, C, Winnipeg Jets
Age: 18 | Draft: 2026 No. 8

It remains to be seen where Bjorck will start his North American professional career, but there is little doubt his future is as a top-six center for the Winnipeg Jets.

Bjorck is a play-driving, get-you-out-of-your-seat player. Whether he's causing turnovers and generating breakaways or outmuscling players much bigger than him, the stocky Swede is going to be a mainstay in the Jets' lineup when he's ready.

If he makes the team out of camp, there is real opportunity for him to slot ahead of Adam Lowry on the second line and have an immediate offensive impact. If he doesn't, his most likely development path is putting in time as the top-line AHL center and a recall after the All-Star break (or as injury necessitates).

He's extremely fun to watch because of his dogged puck pursuit, fearlessness in battles and outright offensive skill. When he's in the lineup, he's going to give Jets fans every reason to be excited, and given Winnipeg's need for a legitimate top-six center, there's an argument that he should start the season with the big club.

Sergei Murashov, G, Pittsburgh Penguins
Age: 22 | Draft: 2022 No. 118

It is extremely rare that a goalie finds himself on a rookie watch list, so that should tell you all you need to know about Murashov's potential. He's one of Pittsburgh's top prospects and is looking to prove his rookie season should be a 1A/1B situation with Arturs Silovs.

There is a legitimate chance that Murashov is the 1A starting goaltender for the Penguins at some point this season, and if that's the case, not only is he a top prospect, but he's also probably in the Calder conversation.

He's a wonderfully charismatic conversationalist off the ice, which is always endearing to fans and media. His mindset and demeanor on the ice are as cool as can be, which has led to sparkling AHL numbers (including a .919 save percentage in 38 starts last season for Wilkes-Barre/Scranton). Add in the intrigue of being a southpaw goaltender capable of spectacular saves, Murashov could be a key piece of Pittsburgh's elongated competitive window. If the Penguins make the playoffs and he plays the lion's share of the games, it will be difficult to keep him out of the Calder discussion.

stories.headline: Toronto Raptors offseason recap, early 2026-27 season preview
stories.summary: With Leonard and Barnes, the Raptors are hoping to bring the franchise back to title contention. Question is: Do they have enough in a stronger East to do it?
stories.body:
The Raptors' road to real Eastern Conference contention opened considerably Monday, when Toronto and the LA Clippers finally hit send on their long-delayed trade that will send seven-time All-Star Kawhi Leonard to Toronto for Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, two unprotected first-round picks, one first-round pick swap and two second-round picks.

The trade ends a saga that enveloped both teams, as the NBA completed its nearly year-long investigation into allegations of salary cap circumvention stemming from the Clippers' dealings with Leonard over the course of his tenure in Los Angeles.

Now with Leonard in Toronto, the two-time Finals MVP will pair with rising star Scottie Barnes and second-year big Collin Murray-Boyles, hoping to replicate the success of their title run in 2019.

ESPN's staff of experts is looking back at the offseason and taking an early look at the 2026-27 season, with 30 previews -- one for every team -- rolling out each weekday through Friday. We're answering the biggest looming questions, evaluating X factors and much more.

Quick links:

Roster | Depth chart | Transactions

More Raptors coverage | More NBA

Offseason at a glance
Key additions: Kawhi Leonard, Kyle Anderson, Andre Jackson Jr.

Key subtractions: Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, Sandro Mamukelashvili

Key retentions: Jamal Shead

After waiting months to finalize their acquisition of Leonard from the Clippers due to the NBA's investigation into salary cap circumvention, the Raptors can finally look ahead to what could be their most promising season in years.

Leonard, who led Toronto to the 2019 championship, plugs in as a major positional upgrade over Ingram. The rest of the Raptors' starting lineup remains intact, and forward Collin Murray-Boyles should only improve after a standout rookie campaign.

While losing Mamukelashvili in free agency took a bite out of their bench unit, Toronto has crafted a high-energy and versatile supporting cast for Leonard and two-time All-Star Scottie Barnes.

The plucky Raptors, who won 46 games last season, have a real shot to win their first playoff series since 2020. -- Ben Golliver

Zach Kram's offseason grade: A

Toronto's only real move of consequence this summer was trading for Kawhi Leonard, who should bring major improvements over Brandon Ingram on both ends -- especially offense, where Leonard is the sort of primary option and half-court scorer that the previous version of the Raptors lacked.

The cost in draft picks was substantially greater than the last time Toronto traded for Leonard, eight years ago, but it was a worthwhile risk for a team that now has a legitimate chance to reach the Finals if Leonard can stay healthy next season. That gamble worked out eight years ago, after all. -- Kram

What we learned this offseason
From Golliver: The Raptors had two good reasons to go through with the Kawhi Leonard trade.

After enjoying a 16-win jump in the standings and snapping a three-year playoff drought, the Raptors entered the summer with a bunch of big contracts on their books and limited avenues to take the next step.

The simplest path to improvement involved packaging either Immanuel Quickley or Brandon Ingram along with other players or picks for positional upgrades. Given the hearty salaries owed to Quickley and Ingram, that wasn't going to be an easy task. But the Raptors managed to construct exactly this type of trade by sending Ingram, Gradey Dick, two first-round picks, a first-round swap and two second-round picks to the LA Clippers for Kawhi Leonard.

The primary goal of the deal, of course, was to bring Leonard back to the organization he led to the 2019 title. With a two-time Finals MVP in place, Toronto could feel much more comfortable against the East's elite and start dreaming about winning its first playoff series since 2020.

The trade's other huge benefit was shedding Ingram's contract. The two-time All-Star disappeared during the 2026 playoffs, and he is owed $40 million in 2026-27 and $41.9 million in 2027-28.

While trading for Ingram in 2025 and subsequently re-signing him were both ill-advised decisions, flipping him for Leonard amounted to a brilliant use of the undo button.

The long-discussed Leonard trade was finally consummated Monday after the NBA completed its investigation into allegations of salary cap circumvention. Once the league office announced that Leonard's punishment was limited to a $700,000 fine, Toronto was able to proceed with a bold move that added talent and fixed a past mistake. -- Golliver

The big question: How high is Scottie Barnes' ceiling?
Barnes' impressive growth shouldn't get lost in all the hubbub over Leonard's arrival.

The 2021 lottery pick really came into his own during his age-24 season, improving his scoring efficiency, earning his first All-Defensive team selection and raising his game against the Cleveland Cavaliers in the playoffs.

While the Raptors lost their first-round series in seven games, Barnes averaged 24.1 points, 6.1 rebounds, 8.6 assists, 1.1 steals and 1.7 blocks per game - a level of all-around playoff production matched only by LeBron James, Nikola Jokic and Cade Cunningham over the past decade.

Barnes should be regarded as one of the leading Defensive Player of the Year candidates, and he just might pop up on future MVP ballots if his upward trajectory and Toronto's winning ways continue. -- Golliver

Basketball Power Index rank: No. 14
Here are the predicted net points per 100 possessions for the Raptors' top seven players for the 2026-27 season:

Kawhi Leonard shot 6.8 three-pointers per game last year, his career high, at 39%, below what he shot in each of the prior four seasons. But the extra volume meant he added plus-1.9 net points per 100 possessions on threes vs plus-1.6 in prior years. That's not a huge bump, but it's relevant.

Also, Leonard is one of those rare players whose college three-point percentage was really low (25%), only to shoot really well in the NBA (39%). -- Dean Oliver

Read about how net points works here.

Biggest X factor this season
PF Collin Murray-Boyles

Ever since the Raptors agreed to acquire Leonard from the Clippers, thoughts of the Leonard/Barnes/Murray-Boyles defensive trio have tantalized. That's the key group and lineup combination that could propel the Raptors to lofty heights next season.

So even though Murray-Boyles is only a second-year player who averaged 8.5 points per game as a rookie, he profiles as one of the biggest X factors in the league.

For the Raptors to maximize their window with Leonard, they need Murray-Boyles to take greater steps next season -- and to prove his bona fides as a smallball center who can replace Jakob Poeltl in clutch situations. -- Kram

stories.headline: Messi tracker: Goals, assists, key moments in 2026
stories.summary: ESPN provides game-by-game analysis of Lionel Messi's performances for Inter Miami and Argentina.
stories.body:
Lionel Messi will aim for more success in 2026. His Inter Miami side captured its first MLS Cup title last season and will look to defend it -- and add further silverware too -- in its first season at Nu Stadium, the club's new home.

Messi also captained Argentina as they fell just one step short of defending their FIFA World Cup crown, losing 1-0 in extra time to Spain in the final of what could be his last tournament.

As the 39-year-old continues to feature for both club and country, ESPN will track his performances game-by-game, providing stats and analysis each time he pulls on a Herons or Albiceleste jersey.

Messi's 2026 tally:

Games played: 37
Goals: 33
Assists: 15

Sep. 16: Inter Miami 2-0 Cruz Azul

Another day, another trophy for Messi.

The Argentine master scored his 100th goal for Inter Miami as the Herons defeated Cruz Azul 2-0 on Wednesday night to win the Campeones Cup.

Messi opened the scoring in the 24th minute, heading in a cross from Luis Suárez, before turning provider for Casemiro -- sending in a corner for the Brazilian to nod home.

Sep. 12: Inter Miami 2-2 Nashville SC
In a matchup between the two best teams in the Eastern Conference, the action went end to end, with Messi getting on the scoresheet for Miami's second goal off a Rodrigo De Paul assist as he continues to lead the Golden Boot race.

Ultimately, the teams settled for a point apiece, as the hosts failed to close the gap on Nashville at the top of the table.

Sep. 9: Chicago Fire 1-1 Inter Miami

Two or Europe's greatest club players took center stage in one of the United States' most iconic American football stadiums on Wednesday -- and a record crowd came out to watch.

Ex-Bayern Munich and Barcelona star Robert Lewandowski scored a trademark acrobatic goal in the 10th minute to give the Fire an early lead at the NFL home of the Chicago Bears.

But Inter Miami drew level shortly after halftime when Casemiro, another of the game's stars with a long history of playing in Europe before moving to MLS, headed home a Messi cross from a corner kick to make it 1-1.

The assist was Messi's league-leading 13th of the season. He also has league 18 goals and is the first player in MLS history with 30-plus goal contributions in three separate seasons.

Sep. 5: Inter Miami 2-2 Atlanta United
Messi was not as effective as he was in the previous matchup, but he did get an assist for Casemiro's opening goal. However, his team was unable to win as they had to settle for a point in a 2-2 draw.

August 29: Inter Miami 7-1 CF Montréal

Fans were treated to a Messi masterclass on Saturday as the Argentine magician registered four goals and an assist to help Miami to a club-record 7-1 victory over CF Montréal.

Messi scored with a deflected free kick in the 40th minute before netting after a stunning solo run in the 52nd. After supplying an assist to Luis Suárez, the 39-year-old then completed his hat trick and with a delicate chip over the goalkeeper with seven minutes of regulation time remaining.

He wasn't done yet.

Deep into stoppage time, Messi lined up a free kick and dispatched it with trademark precision into the top corner of the net. Legendary stuff.

August 22: Inter Miami 2-1 Toronto FC

Messi's 14th MLS goal of the season wasn't enough to prevent Inter Miami from slumping to their fourth loss in their last five games, losing 2-1 to Toronto FC at Nu Stadium on Saturday.

Messi found the net with a first-time finish from a Rodrigo De Paul through-ball with eight minutes remaining, but the home side's late rally fell short of salvaging a much-needed draw to bolster the Herons' pursuit of first-placed Nashville SC in the Eastern Conference.

August 19: Inter Miami 2-2 Philadelphia Union

Messi is back scoring goals, but unfortunately, his Miami side is not back to winning ways. The Argentine scored Miami's second goal of the night as both teams finished with 10 men. Miami are now winless in their last four matches.

August 15: Nashville SC 4-1 Inter Miami
It was not the best night for Messi in Tennessee. The Argentine missed yet another penalty -- his third straight for club and country -- and they suffered a heavy 4-1 loss to their Eastern Conference rivals. However, he did get an assist for Telasco Segovia's equalizer at halftime before Miami lost control in the second half.

August 12: Inter Miami 2-3 Club León
Just days after the passing of his father, Messi came off the bench in the second half to try to help Miami continue in the Leagues Cup after they were leading 1-0. However, it ended in a 3-2 loss which saw them eliminated in the league phase after a second straight loss, coming off defeat to Monterrey last weekend with Messi away at the memorial for his father.

August 5: Inter Miami 4-2 Atlético de San Luis

Lionel Messi made his first start for Inter Miami since returning from the World Cup and picked up right where he left off, scoring a stellar pair of goals to guide his team to a come-from-behind 4-2 rout of Atlético de San Luis in its first game of the 2026 Leagues Cup.

Messi's first goal was an exquisite volley, redirecting Noah Allen's cross from the left flank while running at full speed. Miami's third goal of the opening half -- and Messi's second on the night -- came on the back of some intricate buildup play with Allen once again setting up his team captain, this time in the center of the area where he tiptoed through two defenders and buried a close-range strike past Andrés Sánchez.

The goal made Messi the all-time leading scorer in Leagues Cup history with 14, one ahead of LAFC's Denis Bouanga since the expanded competition began in 2023.

August 1: Inter Miami 2-2 Columbus Crew
Messi made his return to action for Inter Miami on Saturday, 13 days after tasting defeat with Argentina in the World Cup final. The Miami talisman started on the substitutes' bench before being introduced in the 53rd minute of the Herons' 2-2 draw with the Columbus Crew at Nu Stadium in Miami.

July 19: Spain 1-0 AET Argentina

Sunday proved to be a bridge too far for both Messi and Argentina, falling in extra time to Spain in the World Cup final.

With La Roja controlling the match basically from start to finish -- Argentina didn't register a shot on target during regulation time -- Messi had few opportunities to impact the game. Indeed, the 39-year-old was given a 3/10 in ESPN's post-match player ratings.

Still, as Mark Ogden points out, the 2026 tournament was a memorable one for Messi and cemented his status as the GOAT, if it were ever in doubt.

July 15: England 1-2 Argentina
Messi made another statement in his 205th appearance for Argentina, this time in his first-ever match against England in a World Cup semifinal. With so much at stake for both nations, Messi once again proved decisive despite not getting on the scoresheet.

He first provided the assist for Enzo Fernández's superb strike to level the match in the second half before delivering a pinpoint cross for Lautaro Martínez's headed winner, sending the reigning champions into yet another World Cup final after another dramatic encounter.

Messi has now recorded either a goal or an assist in all seven of Argentina's matches at this World Cup, and he will have the opportunity to lift the trophy for a second time when Argentina face Spain in Sunday's final in New Jersey.

July 11: Argentina 3-1 Switzerland
It was a relatively quiet night by Messi's standards as his goalscoring streak came to an end, but his influence on the match stayed the same. He set up Alexis Mac Allister's opening goal for Argentina against Switzerland, and although the match went to extra time, the defending champions won 3-1 thanks to two late goals in the second half of extra time.

Messi's quest to retain the World Cup now continues into the semifinals, where Argentina will face England for the first time in over 20 years. The clash in Atlanta -- one of international soccer's most storied rivalries -- will decide a spot in the final.

July 7: Argentina 3-2 Egypt
It was another dramatic outing for Messi and Argentina, who rallied from a 2-0 deficit to defeat Egypt 3-2 in Atlanta and book their place in the World Cup quarterfinals. As is so often the case, Messi was at the center of the action. Minutes after Egypt opened the scoring, he missed another penalty, but he quickly made amends by setting up Cristian Romero for Argentina's first goal. Messi then scored the equalizer -- his eighth goal of the tournament -- before Enzo Fernández completed the comeback with the winner. Argentina will now face Switzerland in Kansas City for a place in the semifinals.

July 3: Argentina 3-2 Cape Verde
Messi suffered a major scare in Miami Gardens on Friday evening in the round of 32, but it ultimately ended well for Argentina. He opened the scoring with his seventh goal of the tournament, extending his World Cup tally to 20 goals while finding the net in a record eighth consecutive World Cup match. Cape Verde twice fought back -- once in the second half and again in extra time -- but the world champions eventually prevailed 3-2 after extra time to book a meeting in the round of 16 with Egypt.

June 27: Jordan 1-3 Argentina
Messi didn't play the full 90 minutes in Argentina's 3-1 win over an already-eliminated Jordan, but he still made his mark during a 30-minute cameo in Texas. The 39-year-old scored a free kick for his sixth goal of the tournament and his 19th career World Cup goal, becoming the first player ever to score in seven consecutive World Cup matches. Even at 39, he's still got it.

June 22: Argentina 2-0 Austria
Another chapter in an already unparalleled career. Lionel Messi scored twice in Argentina's 2-0 win over Austria to help his team qualify for the round of 32 and become the outright leading goalscorer in men's and women's FIFA World Cup history with 18 goals. After missing an early penalty, he responded by breaking Miroslav Klose's 12-year-old record and then added a second late on to break Marta's record. All just two days before turning 39.

June 16: Argentina 3-0 Algeria
In his 200th appearance for Argentina and sixth World Cup, Lionel Messi sent a message to the world just days before his 39th birthday: he still has it. His first-ever World Cup hat trick powered Argentina to victory in their group-stage opener, while his 16th tournament goal saw him draw level with Miroslav Klose for the most goals in World Cup history.

June 9: Argentina 3-0 Iceland

Messi, working his way back from muscle fatigue ahead of the start of the World Cup, came on in the 70th minute of a pre-tournament friendly in Auburn, Alabama and scored from the penalty spot right afterward.

It was Messi's 911th career goal for club and country and 117th goal for Argentina and made him the oldest scorer in the country's soccer history.

May 24: Inter Miami 6-4 Philadelphia Union

Messi registered two assists in a scintillating performance against Philadelphia on Sunday but, unfortunately, no one was focused on results come the end of the game.

That's because, in the very last game before the World Cup, Messi left the field in the 73rd minute and headed straight to the locker room after grabbing his left thigh.

Now, supporters around the world are holding their collective breath while they wait and see if the injury has scuppered the 38-year-old's chance of appearing at a sixth World Cup.

May 13: FC Cincinnati 3-5 Inter Miami

Two goals and one assist marked yet another spectacular contribution from Miami superstar Messi on Wednesday. The Argentine magician was instrumental as the Herons fought back from 3-2 down to eventually beat Cincinnati 5-3 at TQL Stadium in Ohio.

May 9: Toronto FC 2-4 Inter Miami

It was a day of star power. Not only were Rodrigo De Paul, Luis Suárez and Sergio Reguilón all on the score sheet for the Herons, so was Messi -- and he added a pair of assists, too.

While Miami has yet to taste victory at its new home, it continues to take care of business on the road. Saturday's win in Toronto extended the club's unbeaten record away from home in 2026 to seven games, picking up six wins and one draw in the first few months of the season.

May 2: Inter Miami 3-4 Orlando City

Messi notched a goal and an assist on Saturday in what ended up being an astonishing collapse for Inter Miami at Nu Stadium.

The Herons were leading 3-0 after Messi's classy 33rd-minute strike, but gifted the visitors four goals -- including a Martín Ojeda hat trick -- to once again miss out on a victory at their new home ground. Orlando's comeback from three goals down marks only the third time in MLS history that a team has claimed all three points after trailing by three or more goals.

As for Messi's Miami, only twice has an MLS team had a longer winless run -- now up to four for the Herons -- to open up a new stadium.

April 25: Inter Miami 1-1 New England Revolution
Messi again failed to get on the scoresheet as Miami put in a fatigued second-half performance that saw them come from a goal down against New England. It was another draw -- and another game without a win at their new home, Nu Stadium.

April 22: Real Salt Lake 0-2 Inter Miami
No goals or assists from Messi as Miami visited America First Field on Wednesday, but the fans did get treated to sumptuous strikes nonetheless.

Rodrigo De Paul's opener in the 80th-minute was stunning curler from outside the box and then, almost immediately after the restart, Luis Suarez made it 2-0 with a well-struck volley.

The victory moves Inter Miami into outright second in the MLS Eastern Conference.

April 18: Colorado Rapids 2-3 Inter Miami

Another moment of Messi magic bagged all three points for Inter Miami on Saturday.

With scores level in the 79th minute, the Argentine icon danced his way past a number of Colorado defenders before curling home an outrageous effort into the far corner.

The strike -- Messi's second of the match after converting a penalty in the first half -- helped Miami to their first win under interim coach Guillermo Hoyos.

Hoyos, who had been serving as club's sporting director, took over coaching duties after Javier Mascherano unexpectedly left the club due to personal reasons last week.

April 11: Inter Miami 2-2 Red Bull New York
Miami and Messi are still waiting for a first win at Nu Stadium after a 2-2 draw with Red Bull New York on Saturday night.

Messi didn't register a goal or assist, but did help set up Germán Berterame's second-half strike that gave Inter Miami its first lead at its new home ground, but 17-year-old Adri Mehmeti's first career goal in the 77th minute secured a point for the visitors.

April 4: Inter Miami 2-2 Austin FC
Inter Miami opened Nu Stadium the only way it knows how: With a Messi goal. The No. 10 began the move in trademark style with a left-footed pass to a teammate before moving past a defender and arriving in the box at just the right time to head past goalkeeper Brad Stuver.

March 31: Argentina 5-0 Zambia
It was the last day of the month and perhaps the last game for Messi playing for Argentina playing in his native country, but they put on a show defeating the African side Zambia 5-0. Messi scored the second goal for Lionel Scaloni's side as focus will shift now to Miami until the beginning of the World Cup.

March 27: Argentina 2-1 Mauritania
In his first game for his country in 2026, Messi only played the second half as Argentina won 2-1 against Mauritania at the mythical La Bombonera in Buenos Aires, as the World Cup champions continue to prepare to defend their title this summer in North America.

March 22: NYCFC 2-3 Inter Miami

It was a thrilling encounter in the Bronx, as the Argentine star helped his team to a 3-2 win over NYCFC, which also included another trademark free kick goal, now beginning his course for potentially 1,000 career goals. Only 99 goals left!

March 18: Inter Miami 1-1 Nashville SC

Messi may have made history on Wednesday night, becoming just the second men's player in history to score 900 career goals, but it wasn't enough to seal Miami's progress in the Concacaf Champions Cup.

The Argentina legend found the back of the net in the seventh minute at Chase Stadium, but his strike was cancelled out by Nashville's Cristian Espinoza -- sealing the Herons' tournament exit on the away goals rule.

March 11: Nashville SC 0-0 Inter Miami
A drab night for Messi and Co. in the Concacaf Champions Cup. Plenty of possession but few shots on target mean that the Herons will return to Chase Stadium know a win will be needed to ensure progression.

March 7: D.C. United 1-2 Inter Miami

It was quite an eventful week for Messi. Just days before Miami's match against D.C. United, Messi and the entire squad visited the White House and met President Donald Trump and were eager to put on a show for the sold-out crowd of over 70,000 at Baltimore's M&T Bank Stadium.

And they did just that, with a 2-1 win over D.C. United. Messi, of course, scored Miami's second and is now one goal away from 900 career goals.

March 1: Orlando City 2-4 Inter Miami

Well, that blip didn't last long! Messi and Miami roared back into life with a 4-2 thrashing of Orlando on Sunday thanks to the 38-year-old's wizardry.

Things looked ominous for the Herons after the first 45 minutes, down 2-0 and looking on course to start the MLS season with two bleak losses.

But two goals and an assist from Messi in the second half dragged the visitors back in the game and helped secure Miami their first points of the season.

Feb. 21: LAFC 3-0 Inter Miami
Messi and Miami aimed to start 2026 firing on all cylinders, but it was the hosts who spoiled the defending MLS Cup champions' opener at the LA Coliseum. In front of a sellout crowd of 75,673 -- the second-highest attendance in MLS history -- Miami were outplayed, with LAFC's Denis Bouanga getting a goal and an assist in a convincing home victory.

The main talking point, however, emerged after the final whistle. Messi was initially reported to have gained unauthorized access to the officials' locker room after video circulated showing him near the area. However, it was later reported that no league policy had been violated and Messi was cleared of any wrongdoing. Miami will now turn its attention next weekend against fellow Florida side Orlando City.

stories.headline: 'Deeper connection': Clark finds true self at Warriors
stories.summary: Warriors lock Erin Clark found form and his identity after his move from the battling Gold Coast to become one of the best players in his position in the NRL.
stories.body:
Erin Clark has emerged as one of the game's best locks and Warriors legend Clinton Toopi says it's due to a re-discovery of who he is as a footballer.

The 29-year-old will start in the No.13 jersey against Newcastle in an elimination final at Eden Park on Sunday a transformed footballer, after being chopped and changed by the underperforming Gold Coast outfit for five seasons.

"When he was at the Titans I think Erin lost his identity in terms of who he is," Toopi told AAP.

"Am I a hooker? Am I a lock? Am I a bench player? Psychologically in those moments you are happy to play anywhere, but when given responsibility to own a starting position it's a huge confidence booster.

"Coach Andrew Webster has got the best out of all the players and Erin has shown that he wants to own that lock position."

In the past two seasons at the Warriors, across 50 games, Auckland-born Clark has averaged 135m compared to the 65m he managed at the Titans.

Incredibly he has notched 2686 post-contact metres in two Warriors seasons, well above the 2113m he made in 94 Titans games.

The New Zealand international started his career in the Warriors system and played NSW Cup in the halves. After playing one NRL game for the club he moved to the Titans where he played well but was never offered a regular starting spot.

After one match off the bench for the Warriors last season, he has played the last 49 in the No.13 jersey without missing a game.

"Erin would admit to that deeper connection coming back home for a second time," Toopi said.

"He has spread his wings and come back and flourished to become one of the game's elite and best in terms of what he offers."

While the Warriors players are part of a tightly run system, Clark naturally has attacking gifts that add to the powerful running and aggressive defence in the middle that has made him such a fearsome proposition.

"In his past he was a little nuggety six but didn't get a chance to play at any stage there with the Titans," Toopi said.

"When you play six for a long time it tells you that you have vision, skill and you are a runner.

"What Erin has been able to do at the Warriors is exploit those talents and show what skillset he can bring to the table. You see him go to the line and get short balls away.

"He has got an offload, he powers through, he has got a flick pass. He has got a grubber. He has been given the OK to do that."

Toopi, who suffered the heartbreak of losing the 2002 decider to the Sydney Roosters, explained what was required in a do-or-die final.

"I got caught up in the atmosphere of the 2002 grand final. You walk out on the field and there are 90,000 going crazy and all I could do was be in awe of the moment," Toopi said.

"Before you know it that 80 minutes is over and you have lost a grand final. It still is very raw 20-odd years later. These Warriors boys will want to walk off the field having no regrets at all."
